Sentence (English): An excellent quality-built machine.
Comments (English): [ Design could be so much better ] || ---------------- || An excellent quality-built machine. Five stars all the way for wash/dry performance (on heavy duty cycle with sanitize and dry options, the only cycle I use). For the rest, meh. My previous dishwasher (two rack with full length silverware basket on the side) spoiled me in every respect. It had the most flexible loading system bar none as all tines were adjustable and small grid rack bottoms so any size could go anywhere. High clearance in the bottom rack (13") for my tall things. It was so flexible, I didn't have to pre-stage my dishes to load it, I could just start loading as I readied the dishes, easily repositioning as I went. The Bosch checks almost none of these boxes. With this Bosch I need to pre-stage what dishes I think I can fit and carefully plan my loading, else I'll spend far too much time pulling out and reloading. Clearance is so much less, in all three racks. My tall things won't fit unless I remove the middle rack. The silverware rack isn't tall enough for ladles or other larger utensils so they take up space elsewhere including adding the optional silverware basket while the top rack goes largely unused. The middle rack is height adjustable but with three racks there's not much to work with. There doesn't seem to be a way to quickly cancel a cycle (reset function can be used but takes approximately two minutes). And more. some of those were learning curve for me on operational differences. Less annoying now that I know (like pressing start and having to shut the door within four seconds or start has to be pressed again). Hopefully the annoyance factor will diminish as time passes. To be fair, ALL of the quality built machines I looked at were similar in the "cons" department. So I selected Bosch for the promise of superior wash/dry performance over the others, and so far it hasn't disappointed in that regard.

Sentence (English): The internal racks are hard to load.
Comments (English): [ It's OK ] || ---------------- || The internal racks are hard to load. My old dishwasher was a Maytag and the racks were much easier to load and held more dishes. I like the silverware container, it keeps the pieces separate so they get clean. The third uppermost rack is OK but I don't feel it adds much value. The Stainless cover takes fingerprints easily. My wife found a home brew solution to wipe it with that significantly reduces them. Installation was a little difficult due to the water connection at the dishwasher, make sure this is on and tight before you push the dishwasher into the cabinet. The owners manual could be better and there should be a link to on line videos on how to install and load the dishwasher/

Since it is out of warranty, they tell me to locate any local repair shop to get it fixed. Only issue is, no independent shop will want to touch the dishwasher or any Samsung appliance for that matter. So three years, two dishwashers and $1800 later I need to get a new dishwasher again. To add to the misery, my $4000 Samsung family hub fridge also gave up after only a year plus. I ask the last representative if Samsung is out to loose customers or if they simply do not care. To prove that they are serious, they need to start improving their built quality by a lot and start backing it with a warranty that gives piece of mind.

Sentence (English): I bought this dishwasher online through Costco and the order stated that installation was not available in our area.
Comments (English): [ Dishwasher is good, Costco is not. ] || ---------------- || I bought this dishwasher online through Costco and the order stated that installation was not available in our area. This was fine, as I had already installed several dishwashers in the past and I had prepped the area, including removing the old dishwasher and installing a GFCI outlet from the hardwired connection to the old dishwasher. When the two clowns showed up, they proceeded to attempt to install the dishwasher, assuring me they had done hundreds of these installs. One of them sat on the floor while the other guy tried to install the dishwasher. After a short while, they both abruptly left, not having me sign anything or even saying they had finished. When I looked at what they had done, they had started a short cycle on the dishwasher which seemed to be working fine, but the dishwasher was not installed properly, sticking out from under the counter, they had stripped out one of the screws that secures the dishwasher to the cabinets. I stopped the cycle and found they had left the energy start tag hanging in the dishwasher. Also two screws went missing to install the stainless steel apron underneath. I was able to undo the mess these two clowns made and get the dishwasher installed properly. I also found they had left the operating manuals hanging on the back of the machine when I pulled it out to install it properly. This is unfortunately pretty typical of Costco installers in our area. When they delivered a sectional couch we had ordered, they left some of the feet screwed on crooked which we were left to remedy. I called Customer Service and was offered a $70 refund for my trouble which I feel wasn't really adequate given the colossal missteps by their delivery agents. I'm left trying to find screws to replace the missing ones and out several hours of my time correcting their mistakes. The dishwasher itself is great. We had a Bosch at our old house and we loved it. This is a much more advanced model and except for when it drains you can barely tell the thing is running, it's so quiet. Would recommend the dishwasher highly, would not recommend buying from Costco unless you've had good luck with their installers.

Sentence (English): This dishwasher has had multiple ongoing issues ever since the one-year mark.
Comments (English): [ Do not. ] || ---------------- || This dishwasher has had multiple ongoing issues ever since the one-year mark. The second control panel is broken (but I'm living with it at this point because I can't justify replacing it again. Every few months the dishwasher starts completely shutting off after 14-20 minutes of starting the cycle, and then mysteriously starts working again after a few weeks. No tech has been able to figure out why - the error code says it's blocked but there are no blockages. And now, the lower rack's water wall no longer moves and it looks like its pump will need to be replaced. The amount of time and money I've spent troubleshooting this dishwasher over the past 5 years has far surpassed my tolerance, and in true Samsung form, they offer garbage support. Other online forums seem to agree with me- with the issues I have, my advice is to steer clear of this unit. 3 rounds of Samsung appliances (3 full kitchen and 1 laundry) purchased over 15 years of homeownership in 2 states, and between this and issues with my brand new washing machine, I will not look at another Samsung next time.

Sentence (English): capacity is excellent, 3rd rack design really makes a huge difference.
Comments (English): [ Great capacity, sparkling dishes & dry plastics! ] || ---------------- || Capacity is excellent, 3rd rack design really makes a huge difference. With our old 2-rack dishwasher, clean up after parties would take us 2-3 loads, with this dishwasher we can do it in 1 full load with just a couple of items left over that can easily fit with our next normal load. Even when full to capacity, dishes come out sparkling clean and dry, even plastics! With our old dishwasher, we used to have to shake water out of plastic tupperware, deli & takeout containers, and baby bottles after the cycle was completed and wait hours for the plastics to air dry before unloading them and being able to load the next day's dirty dishes. With this dishwasher, our plastics come out bone dry with just the regular Pro Dry setting (have not had to use high heat or extended Pro Dry, which both take more time), which means we can unload everything as soon as the dishwasher is done running and can start putting in dirty dishes as they are used vs accumulating them on the counters and in the sink. The dishwasher racks slide really smoothly, which was an issue with our old dishwasher even though it also used ball bearings. And also really nice, the dishwasher shows how long the cycle is going to take before you start it, based on the cycle settings selected. So far we've had the dishwasher for a little over a month and run every night. No issues so far, and maintenance looks like it should be trivial since it has self cleaning filters. Overall, very happy customers with clean and dry dishes!

Sentence (English): I was debating whether to buy a dishwasher because it was for three people, but I really wanted one, so I ordered a pretty but affordable Minix dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ The only thing I regret about the Mutagong Gamsung dishwasher is that I bought it too late. ] || ---------------- || I was debating whether to buy a dishwasher because it was for three people, but I really wanted one, so I ordered a pretty but affordable Minix dishwasher. I've been using it for a few days now, and I'm so sorry I waited so long to buy one. I'll share my actual experience and summarize all the questions I had before purchasing. Pros 1. Cleanliness without a plate. My kitchen cabinets are small and awkward, so I was hesitant to buy a dishwasher because I thought it wouldn't work if I removed any more cabinets. But I really wanted one, so I bought it. And since it's a plateless dishwasher, it leaves no traces in the house, so it's super clean and tidy. You don't have to remove cabinets, so I recommend measuring the size before purchasing. 2. Convenience: It's convenient because it's for three people, so I think everyone knows it has a small capacity. Everyone knows that it's important to have a larger capacity, but what if I don't have enough space? Is it really convenient for it to do the dishes I would do in 30 minutes in one or two hours? I thought about this until right before purchasing. And the result was, why did I buy it so late? Evenings are precious, so it's hard to wash all the dishes when all you need to do is just wash the pots. It's not a huge deal, but it saves time and allows you to do other things. 3. Its incredible cleaning power. It also dries the dishes, and seeing them sparkle clean after washing is incredibly satisfying. I recommend buying the detergent before the dishwasher. Cons: 1. It's quite noisy. People say you get used to it, but it's noticeable once you get used to it, and it's not so noisy that you can ignore it. However, since we always have the TV on, I think the convenience outweighs the noise. 2. Storage? Unless it's 24-hour storage, there's an auto-open door, but many reviews say it smells like water, so you have to open the door right away. You can't go to sleep until it's finished, so you have to open the dishwasher door quickly. It's like having a dryer running at night and not being able to sleep. 3. Small room size: The biggest problem with the small size of the unit for three people is the location. I'm always agonizing over where to place the ladle and the bowl, and sometimes I find myself thinking, "Wouldn't it be better to spend this time doing the dishes?" While there are more drawbacks than you might think, the one advantage that outweighs them all is convenience. The ability to spend the time washing dishes on other things is what makes me recommend this product without any regrets!

Comments (English): [ I bought this dishwasher after much consideration, and I have no regrets. ] || ---------------- || 1. Which should I choose, the 12-place setting or the 6-place setting? I used to use a 12-place setting built-in dishwasher. Now that my children are all grown up and I don't have many dishes unless it's a special occasion, I don't really need it anymore. Also, bending down to put dishes in and take them out was inconvenient, so I decided to buy a 6-place setting dishwasher when I moved. 2. Which company's model should I choose? I looked at models from Samsung, Google, and Coupang, but the 6-place setting models had a single-tier structure instead of a two-tier one. I was planning to buy a two-tier S*Magic product, but I heard they withdrew from the business and are no longer producing it. While searching, I found that Media was the manufacturer. I hesitated because I was worried about after-sales service, but I decided to choose this one because Coupang offered a free 2-year warranty. 3. Advantages: - This product allows you to remove the top tier and use it with large dishes placed in the bottom tier. - Both the top and bottom plates are made of stainless steel. - It has washing blades on both the top and bottom, so the cleaning power is excellent. This is the most important part; it washes glass dishes especially clean and clear. - It has a better aesthetic appeal than the products used at my friends' and family's homes. - The controls are intuitive. - It has an automatic door opening function, so it opens on its own if I forget about it, which is great. - It says to use 7 grams of detergent, but even cutting a 1/3 of a bottle of Frosh detergent into the container works well for cleaning. The detergent container looked a bit awkward at first, but it is not inconvenient to use. - There were reviews saying the noise was loud, but it isn't that bothersome. It is probably louder than a built-in model, though. - I was worried about the lack of a hot air drying function, but leaving the door open for a few hours dries the dishes well, so there is no inconvenience. - I chose the ivory color; it is a subtle shade that looks 고급 and matches well. - It doesn't take up much space. 4. Cons. - The cutlery holder is small. - The space is somewhat cramped. Thanks to that, I think my Tetris skills for stacking dishes neatly will improve. ^^ 5. Usage Tips. I rinse off food scraps with water or soak the dishes in water before putting them in the dishwasher to wash once it is full. Some people just put them in, but even though there is a filter, I do this to avoid potential malfunctions. I am a long-time Coupang customer and a frequent user of Rocket Fresh, but this is the first time I am leaving a long review for a product I purchased with my own money. I recommend this to anyone who is hesitating like I was. It has only been two days, so I need to use it more, but as long as it doesn't break down, it is a really good product. ## 2-Month Review. I use it once a day. My kitchen has become cleaner, and most importantly, my dishes are sparkling clean. After dinner, I put everything in together and run the cycle while I do other things. Once the 65-degree wash is finished, the door opens automatically, and I leave it wide open for drying. I love how fresh and fluffy the dishes are in the morning. They look pristine when I put them straight into the cupboard in the morning. I wonder why I didn't buy this sooner. They say there is a lottery involved with electronics, but perhaps I got a good one, as I am using it very well and recommending it to those around me. The price has even dropped since I purchased it. I highly recommend this to anyone who is still undecided.

Cons. - The cutlery holder is small. - The space is somewhat cramped. Thanks to that, I think my Tetris skills for stacking dishes neatly will improve. ^^ 5. Usage Tips. Sentence (English): I recently moved and purchased this dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ A good dishwasher one small step from great ] || ---------------- || I recently moved and purchased this dishwasher. In my previous home, I had a ~1 year old top of the line Maytag unit. TL;DR: Really, this is a great dishwasher that is quiet, looks good, and generally does a good job of cleaning my dishes, with the exception of some random silverware pieces. Pros: - This dishwasher is very quiet! I can hardly hear it when we sit 5 feet away in the living room. - Though this is subjective, I prefer the appearance of this unit. - The display on the front is great; I can easily see time remaining. It doesn't look cheap, either. - Having a light inside is a feature that I didn't know I needed! - The small 3rd rack that can handle silverware is nice and means I can often take the silverware basket out of the bottom rack. - The tines on the middle and lower rack fold down in several groups, making it easier to accommodate large/awkward items.Cons: - Especially when I have the top (silverware) rack more than 1/2 full, I often get food redeposited (and then subsequently baked/dried) onto the silverware, requiring another wash. - Similarly, when it is more full, I often get food redeposited onto clean dishes, requiring a second wash. - Compared to my true 3-rack Maytag, the capacity is notably less. The Maytag could fit cups, bowls, and large utensils on the top rack; this unit really only fits silverware and some pancake turners and such. Neutral: - Having wi-fi is a nice touch, though mostly unnecessary. I almost exclusively run the unit overnight (cheaper energy) so I don't need notified when it is complete.

Comments (English): [ Samsung for Life - Great Products ] || ---------------- || I purchased another great Samsung product. My home is and has been a Samsung home for many years and have changes with Samsung as newer and more advanced products have evolved through technological advances. I think it's the quality of the product that keeps us coming back for more items and replacing items as they all eventually will wear out and I want the best and will make a change even when you have something that is in perfect working order. I make purchases based on life of the items and what sales are available to me. The other great thing about Samsung is their discounts to veterans and they customer service. I am not saying that you have a great experience every time, because it just doesn't happen. But I if you are consistent and know the products it's an easier path. Be and stay informed and don't stop engaging customer service if you feel like you are in the "RIGHT", frame of mind and rights of a customer who has an that slipped through the and made into inventory. SDo it didn't need to be replaced as it was not a major issue now. Now how many wives are out there that are going to let you not continue with the purchase of a new appliance especially around Christmas so we replaced it. The biggest issue that I have had is not necessarily a direct Samsung problem with their products. It's whom they are using as installers, repairing and servicing, and or delivering their product's. I hope that they address this issue so that we have less issues because it's a Samsung vendor and not the quality of the product that is the problem and creates bad impressions and reviews because of the vendor and not the product. it's hard to be positive when it comes damaged during shipping and installation it's not the quality of the product but who wants a damaged item or one that is not functionionalty working properly due to an installation issue. I have had a lemon and worked through the process and got a satisfactory resolution. We are in our living life and don't think about the products that we are using because their have quality and a long life so we just use them through our daily routine and just don't think about as we wash and dry our clothes, feed our family on Samsung's kitchen appliances and relaxation with their line of entertainment and gaming application's. I am proud to be a part of the Samsung enviromnet and looking for the next new thing,What's next and thank you Samsung.

Sentence (English): We came to the Bosch 800 having had 12 miserable years (should've changed earlier, I know! )

It is whisper quiet which is a very nice improvement over the Whirlpool. The cleaning quality has been superb, even with baked and fried-on food. No leaks, as expected. One benefit we love and didn't necessarily expect to get after reading reviews is the Bosch 800 does a better job of drying than the Whirlpool did, including the many plastics our family uses. My only knock is the non-standard installation vs most other dishwashers being corded and not hard-wired, so that led to another purchase and more wait time to install as I had to order the hard-wiring kit, which if you have no cabinet access next to the dishwasher is also a bit of a hassle to manage, since it is supposed to be mounted in an adjoining cabinet for easier access to the wiring. Not a showstopper by any means, but not ideal. Overall we are very happy and would purchase the same unit again!

The tines are so close together that many of our dishes don't fit, such as bowls. The tines are not vertical so washing things like tall tumblers makes them fall over and not get washed properly, but they're too tall for the middle rack. As far as rinsing, the leftover rinse water that accumulates and pools on flat dish surfaces seems very cloudy and dirty compared to my previous model, and that's when using rinse aid and the special dishwasher salt with the proper amount of softening levels applied per the manual's directions. It's gross. The good - It does clean dishes, as all dishwashers do. I also like the physical buttons which are better than capacitance touch buttons that some appliances have. Overall, this is a very annoying dishwasher that lacks basic features that have been around for decades, and doesn't seem to clean as well as a cheap dishwasher. We do like the idea of the leak protection because that's what went wrong with our previous dishwasher and caused lots of damage, so we're hoping to avoid that with this Bosch. So far, we regret this purchase and it seems like a major downgrade. We feel that it performs in a class of dishwashers selling for half of this price.

Sentence (English): We had an installation scheduling issue that resulted in Costco offering us a $25 gift card.
Comments (English): [ Doesn't seem fair. ] || ---------------- || We had an installation scheduling issue that resulted in Costco offering us a $25 gift card. Two weeks after installation the dishwasher started leaking from the door on to our floor. Also washed about 4 times, 2 of those times the dishwasher wouldn't complete the washing cycle leaving standing water inside the dishwasher. After one month we called Costco to return the unit for a full refund. We discovered that Costco deducted the $25 gift card amount from our refund. At no point were we ever advised that this would happen. We contested this saying it was a gift that Costco said they would give us because of the installation issue, we didn't ask for it. We returned the dishwasher because it was defective. We ordered a different replacement dishwasher from Costco because the first model was no longer available. Costco offered to give us another $25 gift card to offset the $25 short refund from the first dishwasher we returned. But they also advised us that if we returned the second dishwasher, they would deduct the $25 second gift card from our refund. We hope we never have to return the second dishwasher. The handling of the refund isn't fair. We asked the customer service Costco person to address it with their supervisor, the result didn't change. A full refund is the purchase price. You don't deduct a gift card from it for two different issues, an installation problem for the gift card versus a full refund for a defective product.

Comments (English): This is a review written after receiving the product for free as part of the Coupang Experience Group event. Dishwasher Auntie ~~ Come and see for yourself ~ We have three children, and the youngest is a mom who hasn't even turned one yet, so she cries and makes a fuss if I stay in the kitchen for too long, so I can barely cook and I can't do the dishes at all. It was annoying to wash the dishes that had barely piled up while the baby was sleeping. I wanted to rest but I had to do the dishes, so I got really annoyed. That's why I really needed a dishwasher, so I chose this one. Products that are too big are burdensome, but this product is not that small. The interior is spacious. It can hold a lot of dishes. I was surprised, and the installation was done quickly. The selection was a mess, so I did it myself. They said I had to clean the water hose myself. That part was a bit disappointing. The installation didn't feel perfect. The finishing was a bit disappointing, but the dishwasher works well. I ate pork belly and all the grease was gone. This is amazing. When I wash the dishes myself, I wipe the pork belly plate****** and wipe it several times, but I just put the dishwasher right in and it was spotless. The kids' plates were a mess because the rice was dried on them, but they were all cleaned up. The spoons were shiny. I now know why they call it the dishwasher aunt. I love it. The price is not too expensive, so it's not a big burden. If you're looking for an inexpensive, high-performance dishwasher, I recommend it.

Comments (English): [ I bought this to use exclusively for the baby, such as baby bottles, after giving birth. ] || ---------------- || This is a review written after using the product for about three months since its installation on October 9th. I purchased this before my baby was born to sterilize baby bottles and use it exclusively for baby-related items. I intend to run it exclusively for baby-related tasks. I have run it with baby bottles and clean, contaminated glass plates or bowls. Going forward, this dishwasher will handle the washing up that will come with introducing solid foods. Regarding after-sales service and estimated product lifespan: The product warranty is 1 year, the parts retention period is 5 years, and two core motor components are covered by warranties of 3 and 10 years. I chose this dishwasher with the intention of using it for about 4 to 5 years, and I am satisfied with both the price and performance. Since it is a new model and the parts retention period is up to 5 years, I decided to consider that to be a significant amount of use. 1. Installation: All the installation technicians were kind, and they called me between 7 PM and 8 PM the day before installation. They kept their appointments well, and most importantly, they installed it meticulously and explained how to use it. They installed it with a microfiber cloth placed on the floor to prevent scratches or dents. We opted for a drilled installation; although it would have been possible to run the wires through the baseboard under the sink without drilling, they advised that we would need to drill into the drawers or similar areas to secure the wires. So, we drilled into the sink. Before purchasing, I measured the dimensions and secured a spot before ordering. I installed it away from the gas stove, and while it turned out to be larger than expected, I am satisfied. 2. Background of Purchase. With childbirth approaching, I debated whether to buy a U-Pang or a dedicated steam sterilizer for baby bottles, or to purchase a small dishwasher to use for a long time. Boiling water sterilization is recommended for newborn bottles for at least 100 days, so that was another concern. Ultimately, after much deliberation, I purchased a dishwasher and am using it well. Before buying, I compared it with a product from Brand L, and I chose this one because it is hygienic; the interior of the dishwasher, excluding the bottom section, is made of stainless steel. The upper interior of Brand L's dishwasher was not stainless steel! 3. The cycle and method used for washing bottles (see photo). Plus some TMI. First, I gathered all the bottles at once and ran about 8 of them. I kept the used bottles in a washing container filled with detergent. I ran the dishwasher about 1-2 times a day, pre-washing them before putting them in. Since I was also pumping for mixed feeding, the dishwashing was no joke. (Is it just breast milk?). Newborns produce a huge amount of bottles, so I put them in the dishwasher and ran it, and also did boiling water sterilization once a day. I heard that dishwasher sterilization involves rinsing and drying at a total temperature of 75 degrees, so since my baby was a newborn, I also regularly sterilized the bottles in boiling water at 100 degrees. I am doing this in parallel because my baby is not yet 100 days old. (After the baby was 80 days old, I used dishwasher-washed bottles up to twice, and for the third use, I sterilized the washed bottles in boiling water. After 100 days, I plan to increase the frequency to 1-2 times a week for boiling water sterilization.) I calculated the time it takes for the dishwasher to run and the bottles to air dry. I had 9 bottles (160-200ml capacity) on hand, and 3 of them were large Lansino bottles (240ml). When the amount of formula I prepared per feeding was around 165ml, I just used them together, so I used a total of 12 bottles. As the baby grew and the intervals between feedings increased to 5-6 times a day, I think I ended up washing the bottles every two days. In the beginning, when I used a lot of bottles, if the bottles weren't completely dry after the dishwasher run and I was in a hurry, I would run the dishwasher, pour boiling water from a formula kettle into the bottles and nipples to rinse them once, and then warm up formula or pumped breast milk to feed them. I used Spectra bottles at the postpartum care center, so to ensure my baby wouldn't have trouble adjusting to the nipples when we came home, I used Spectra bottles and a breast pump (for mixed feeding). I also used Lansinoh glass bottles. Glass bottles tend to dry quickly and get nice and warm. (I plan to switch to glass bottles when I upgrade the model.) I used Mother-K liquid dishwasher detergent. On days when I did a thorough pre-wash, I used the rapid mode (29 minutes) and added an extra rinse (available once). (I also frequently use the combination of rapid + high-temperature sterilization + powerful drying; it takes 71 minutes). After the wash cycle finished, I selected the bottle sterilization cycle (a function that does not add detergent). On days when I did a pre-wash almost as well as a full wash? I sometimes just ran the bottle sterilization cycle plus an extra rinse (53 minutes), and this cycle does not add detergent separately. So, if I had washed the bottles thoroughly in the sink, I would either run the bottle sterilization cycle instead of the boiling water sterilization cycle, or I would do a quick pre-wash, select a rapid or standard wash cycle to clean the bottles, and then run the sterilization cycle again once finished. When I was feeling lazy, I would run the standard cycle (68 minutes) and add the powerful drying cycle. Tip! If you select the drying mode, pause it briefly after the wash is finished, open the door to shake off the water from the bottles, nipples, and accessories in the basket, and then run the drying cycle; they will be much drier then. Once it finishes, open the door a little later to take them out, move them to a drying rack, and air dry them naturally for faster drying. I put nipples and consumables in a separate basket because they tend to fly around inside when running. Since they don't dry completely after the cycle, I transferred them to a drying rack to air dry before using them again. Advantages: High-temperature sterilization is possible (however, high-temperature sterilization cannot be selected for the bottle or drum sterilization cycles). You can wash all baby items inside (make sure to check if the cycle is dishwasher-safe before putting items in; otherwise, they will shrink). If you put dishes in and use the powerful drying function, they dry well (curved items might retain some moisture inside, but everything else dries well and feels nice and warm). The door opens automatically after the wash is finished (some models do not open automatically, but the Bespoke model does). It is suitable for washing dishes left over after a meal for two. It didn't hold that little. (Glass food containers, clean dishes, cutlery, etc. I sometimes sterilize items with hot water, but I tried putting them in the dishwasher after a pre-wash a few times and it was fine. I checked how much it actually holds). It seems like it will be useful for washing baby food dishes and things like that. After about 20 uses, an alarm automatically pops up on the dishwasher display saying that drum sterilization is needed, and it is hygienic because it has a drum sterilization function (some models do not display this). Once the dishwasher finishes, the liquid detergent dispenser opens automatically (some models do not open). The noise level is not loud by my standards. The dishwasher basket comes out easily as a whole, and there is no difficulty putting it back in (some models are difficult to clean the inside because they don't come out or fit together well). Downside: Nowadays, they don't provide paper manuals; I downloaded the manual via the single-page QR code provided. I think it might be a bit difficult for elderly people to familiarize themselves with how to use it. Also, before purchasing, I was debating between a model with a hot air drying function (DW30CB300C model) and the model I have now installed. I ended up buying this one. Sometimes I wish it had a function to dry things thoroughly. I do wonder if I should have bought a different model. (But I heard that other models are almost the same and don't dry things thoroughly). Still, since it has a drying function, dishes with wide surfaces are mostly dry. (PPSU bottles don't dry all the way through, so you need to move them to a separate drying rack.) In my experience, moisture stays inside the dishwasher for a long time. Even when I leave the door open, I have to leave it open for several days for the inside to dry completely. (If you use it every day, you might not mind; since I only run the baby's items these days and only use it once every two days, the moisture bothered me.) I don't think the large dishwasher I used before was like this, so maybe it's because this is a small one. Overall, I am satisfied with it. Additional review after the baby turned 100 days. First, I do boiling water sterilization once a week these days. Then, I roughly wash things and use the Standard + High Temperature Sterilization + Extra Rinse + Power Dry (takes 1 hour and 41 minutes) cycle the most. I hardly use the separate bottle sterilization course anymore. I run it for everything related to the baby, such as bottles, teething toys, and pacifiers. I run the dishwasher once every 2 to 3 days. (Feeding intervals are 4 hours, using 4 bottles a day). When the dishwasher starts and there are 30 minutes left, it is the "Power Dry" time. It doesn't blow hot air or a breeze; instead, it works like a hair dryer. The principle is that water at a high temperature of over 70 degrees is sprayed, and that heat is transferred to the dishes to dry them. Dishes, plates, and glass, which retain thermal energy well, dry quickly, but plastics do not. (I checked the post on the Samsung Electronics website asking how to dry them well). I stop the dishwasher when there are 10 to 15 minutes left on the Power Dry timer. When I open the door, a lot of hot steam comes out. I organize the nipples, accessories, and bottles inside (shake off the water), put them back in properly, and press start. Once it is finished, the dishwasher door opens, and I move the items to the bottle drying rack to air dry. I wanted to share this in case anyone thought Power Dry just blows out air. No matter how much I think about it, I feel like I made the right purchase for my needs! Good luck with parenting! April 7, 2025 [Updated Review] The baby is over 172 days old (approaching 6 months). I have uploaded additional photos. I am reverently preparing and practicing solid foods. Why are there so many containers and tools? It is very, very good. I really think I made a great purchase! Bottles, teething toys, pacifiers, silicone medicine bottles, and even sucking toys made of dishwasher-safe materials—I put everything in there to wash and sterilize it. I am satisfied! If my honest review of a product I bought with my own money was helpful, please press the like button~
Comments (Original): [ 출산후 젖병 등 아기전용으로 쓰려고 구매함. ] || ---------------- || 10월 9일에 설치하고, 3개월 정도 사용하고 쓰는 후기입니다.아기가 태어나기 전에 젖병살균소독 및 아기 전용으로 쓰려고 구매했어요. 온리 아기에 관련된 것만 돌리려고 합니다.젖병과 오염물질이 없는 깨끗한 유리 접시나 그릇 등 넣어서 돌렸구요. 앞으로는 이유식 하면서 나올 설거지들을 요 식세기가 담당할 예정입니다. ✅️AS 및 제품 사용 예상 기간 제품 보증기간 1년,그외 주품 보유기간 5년, 핵심부품 모터 2종(3년, 10년) 보증. 한 4~5년 정도 쓰면 많이 사용한거라 생각하고, 그 정도 쓸 용도로 고른 식세기인데 가격도 성능도 만족합니다.신형모델이고, 부품 보유기간이 최대 5년이라.. 이정도 쓰면 많이 쓴거다 생각하기로 했습니다. ✅️1. 설치설치 기사님 모두 친절하셨고, 설치 전날 19~20시 사이에 해피콜 왔었어요.시간약속도 잘지켜주시고 무엇보다 설치 꼼꼼하게 잘해주시고 사용법도 설명해주셨습니다. 바닥이 긁히거나 찍힘 방지 위해 바닥에 융 같은거 깔아서 설치 해주셨습니다. 저희는 타공으로 설치했는데, 싱크대 하부에 걸래받이 쪽으로 선을 빼서 무타공도 가능했으나, 그 선을 고정해야되서 서랍장 등에 일부 타공해야 된다고 하시더라구요. 그래서 싱크대를 타공했습니다. 구매하기 전에 미리 사이즈 측정하고, 놓을 자리 확보 후에 주문했어요.가스렌지와 떨어진 곳에 설치했고, 다 설치하고 보니 생각보다 사이즈가 컸지만, 만족합니다. ✅️2. 구매배경출산을 앞두고, 유팡이나 젖병전용 스팀 소독기 등을 구매할지..  아니면, 소형 식세기를 구매해서 오래 쓸지 고민했어요. 신생아 젖병은 열탕소독을 최소 100일 까지 권장하는데.. 그런 부분도 고민이 되었구요. 결국은 고민 끝에, 식세기를 구매했고, 잘쓰고 있습니다. 구매전에 L사의 제품과 비교했는데 이 제품을 선택한 사유는 식기세척기 내부 하단제외 나머지 부분이 스테인리스로 되어있어서 위생적이라 구매했습니다.  L사 제품은 식세기내부 윗부분이 스테인리스가 아니더라구요!!✅️3. 젖병세척시 사용했던 코스 및 방법(사진참조) 그외 TMI먼저 저는 젖병을 한번에 모아서 8개 정도 돌렸어요.  사용한 젖병은 세제풀어둔 세척통에 넣어놨었고,하루에 1~2번 정도 식세기로 돌렸는데, 애벌세척 후 식세기 안으로 넣었어요. 혼합수유 유축도해서.. 설거지가 장난아니 였습니다.. (모유가 뭐길래..)신생아 때는 젖병이 진짜 많이 나와요ㅜ 그래서 식세기 넣코 돌리고, 열탕소독 1일 1회 했습니다.식세기로의 살균이 총 75도로 헹구고 건조해주는거라고 해서, 신생아라.. 정기적으로 100도 팔팔 끓는 물에 젖병들 열탕소독도 해줬습니다. 아직 아기가 100일이 안되어서 병행하고 있습니다. (생후 80일 지나고 부턴 2번까지 젖병 식세기 돌린걸로 쓰고, 3번째 쓸때는 세척된 젖병들 열탕소독 함, 100일 지나면 주 1~2회 정도로 텀 늘려서 열탕소독 예정)식세기 돌아가고 자연건조 되는 시간. 고려해서 돌렸었구요. 젖병 9개(160~200ml용량) 구비했고, 3개는 란시노 큰거(240ml)인데 1회 분유타는 량이 165ml 정도로 되었을땐 걍 같이 써서 젖병 총 12개 사용했습니다. 애기가 커서 하루 5~6번 수유로 텀이 늘다보니 2일에 1번으로 젖병 세척돌리게 된거 같아요.초반에 젖병 많이 쓸때는.. 식세기 돌리고 젖병 건조가 덜되서 급할땐 식세기 돌아가고 분유포트 끓인물 젖병이랑 젖꼭지에 넣코 한번 헹구고 분유나 유축모유 데워서 줬어요.저는 조리원에서 스펙트라 젖병을 써서 아기 집에왔을때 젖꼭지 적응 힘들지 말라고 스펙트라 젖병이랑 유축기(혼합수유함) 썼어요.그리고 같이 란시노 유리젖병도 썼습니다.  유리젖병은 빨리 마르는 편이고 뜨끈뜨끈 합니다. (단계업하면 다 유리젖병으로 교체예정)세제는 마더케이 액상식세기 세제 사용했습니다. 꼼꼼하게 애벌세척을 했던 날은, 급속모드(29분)를 사용하고 헹굼추가(1회 가능)를 했습니다. (급속+고온살균+강력건조 이 조합도 잘씀 71분 뜸)그리고 나서 세척 코스가 끝나면, 그 다음 젖병살균코스(세제투입 안되는 기능임)를 선택했어요. 애벌세척을 거의 세척급으로 잘한날은?그냥 젖병살균코스+헹굼추가(53분)만 돌리기도 했는데, 이 코스는 세제가 따로 투입되거나 하지 않아요.그래서 따로 싱크대에서 세척을 잘 했으면, 젖병살균 코스만 열탕소독 대신 개념으로 돌리던가, 아니면 애벌세척 대충하고, 급속이나 표준으로 세척코스를 선택해 젖병을 씻고, 끝나면 다시 살균코스를 돌리는 방법을 택했습니다.영 귀찮을땐, 표준(68분)으로 돌리고, 강력건조를 추가했어요. 팁!! 건조모드 선택하면 세척 끝나면 그때 잠시 정지 후 열고 젖병이랑 젖꼭지 부속품들 바스켓에 넣어둔거 물기 탈탈 털어주고 건조모드 돌리면 그나마 많이 말라있어요. 종료되면 문 좀 늦게 열고 꺼내서 젖병 건조대 이동 후 자연 건조시 빨리 마름.젖꼭지나 소모품은 돌리면 여기저기 내부에서 튀어다녀서 별도 바스켓에 넣어서 돌렸어요. 다 돌아가고 나면 뽀송하게 바싹 안마르기 때문에 따로 건조대로 옮겨서 말려주고 사용했습니다. ✅️장점고온살균이 가능해요. (단 젖병살균 통살균 코스로는 고온살균이 선택이 안됩니다)아기 용품들 다 넣어서 세척이 가능해요(넣기전에 식세기 사용해도 되는 코스인지 꼭 확인하고 돌리세요. 안그러면서 쪼그라듭니다. )그릇 등 넣고 강력건조 기능쓰면 잘 말라요.(굴곡진 것들은 안에 물기가 좀 남아있고, 그 외에는 잘 말라있음 뜨끈뜨끈함)세척이 끝나고 자동으로 문이 열려요(일부 안열리는 모델들이 있음, 비스포크는 열림)2인 식사후 나오는 그릇 등 세척하기에 적합해요. 그렇케 조금 들어가지 않았어요. (유리 락앤락 반찬통들, 깨끗한 그릇들, 수저 식기류들 등.. 가끔 뜨거운물로 소독하는데, 애벌세척 후 식세기에 넣어서 몇번 써보니까 괜찮았어요. 얼마나 들어가나 봄)이유식 그릇 등 돌릴때 유용할꺼 같습니다. 20회 정도 사용하고 나면, 식세기 디스플레이에 자동으로 통살균 필요하다고 알람이 뜨고 통살균 기능이 있어서 위생적이에요.(안뜨는 기기들도 있음.)식세기 다 돌아가고 나면 액상 세제 투입기가 자동으로 열려있음 (안열리는 모델도 있음)소음이 내기준 크지 않음. 식세기 바스켓 통째로 잘빼지고 다시 끼는데 어려움 없음.( 잘 안빼지고 안껴져서 내부 청소하기 힘든 모델들이 있음..)✅️단점설명서가 요즘은 종이로 안줌, 주신 한장짜리 큐알 들어가서 설명서 다운받았어요. 어르신들이 사용법을 숙지하시기에는 좀 어려움이 있으실꺼 같습니다. 또 구매전에 열풍건조기능이 있는 제품(DW30CB300C모델)이랑 지금 설치한 모델이랑 고민을 했었는데.. 이거로 구매했고.가끔 바싹 말려주는 기능이 있으면 좋켔다.. 다른 모델로 샀으면 어땠을까? 생각이 들긴하더라구요. (근데 다른 모델도 거의 똑같데요 바싹 안말려준데요)그래도 건조기능이 있어서 표면이 넓은 그릇들은 거의 말라있긴 합니다. (ppsu 젖병은 속까지 안말라요.. 따로 건조대 이동 필요함)식세기 기기 내부에 물기가 내기준 오래 있어요. 문열고 있어도 몇일을 열어놔야 안이 바싹 마르더라구요... (매일 쓰면 신경 안쓸 수 있음, 요즘 애기꺼만 돌리다보니 2일에 1회 써서 물기들이 신경쓰였음) 이전에 쓰던 대형 식세기는 안그랬던거 같은데, 소형이라 그런가봐요;;전반적으로 만족하며 사용하고 있습니다.✅️ 아기 100일  지나고 추가후기우선 요즘 열탕소독을 주1회 합니다.그리고 대강 씻어서 표준+고온살균+헹굼추가+강력건조( 1시간 41분 뜸)를. 제일 많이 씁니다. 따로 젖병살균코스는 이제 거의 안쓰게 되네용. 젖병 치발기 쪽쪽이 애기에 대한거 다 돌립니다. 2~3일에 1번씩 식세기 돌려요. (수유텀 4시간, 젖병 1일 4병 사용함)식세기 돌아가고 마지막 30분 남았을때 강력건조 시간인데건조 열풍이나 바람이 나오는게 아니고, 드라이기 말리는 형식으로, 고온 70도 이상물이 뿌려지고 그 열기가 식기로 전달되어 건조되는 원리랍니다. 열에너지를 잘가지고 있는 그릇 접시 유리들은 빨리건조되고, 플라스틱 들은 그렇치 못해요ㅜ.ㅜ .(삼성전자 사이트에서 건조가 잘되는법을 알려주세요 글 확인함)강력건조한 건조시간 10~15분 남았을때 정지 후. 문열면 뜨거운 김, 수증기가 많이 나와요. 안에 젖꼭지 부속품들 젖병 등 정리(물기털기)를 하고 다시 바르게 넣코 시작 누른 뒤. 다 끝나면 식세기 문이 열리고, 젖병건조대로 옮겨서 자연건조 시키고 있어용.혹시 강력건조가 바람나온다고 생각하실까봐 공유드리구요.계속 생각해도 목적에 맞게 잘산거 같아요!육아 홧팅입니다!✅️ 25년 4월 7일 추가후기 아기는 생후 172일 넘음 (6개월 되어감) 추가사진 업로드함.이유식을 경건하게 준비 및 연습하는데.. 이유식 용기들 도구들 왜케 많이나오죠.. 매우 매우 좋습니다. 진짜 잘산거 같아요!젖병들도 치발기 쪽쪽이 실리콘약병.. 식세기 넣어도 되는 소재의 빠는 장난감들.. 모두모두 잘 넣어서 씻고 살균합니다. 만족합니다! 저의 내돈내산 솔찍 리뷰가 도움 되셨다면 좋아요 꾸욱 눌러주세요~❤️

Sentence (English): I purchased this before my baby was born to sterilize baby bottles and use it exclusively for baby-related items.
Comments (English): [ I bought this to use exclusively for the baby, such as baby bottles, after giving birth. ] || ---------------- || This is a review written after using the product for about three months since its installation on October 9th. I purchased this before my baby was born to sterilize baby bottles and use it exclusively for baby-related items. I intend to run it exclusively for baby-related tasks. I have run it with baby bottles and clean, contaminated glass plates or bowls. Going forward, this dishwasher will handle the washing up that will come with introducing solid foods. Regarding after-sales service and estimated product lifespan: The product warranty is 1 year, the parts retention period is 5 years, and two core motor components are covered by warranties of 3 and 10 years. I chose this dishwasher with the intention of using it for about 4 to 5 years, and I am satisfied with both the price and performance. Since it is a new model and the parts retention period is up to 5 years, I decided to consider that to be a significant amount of use. 1. Installation: All the installation technicians were kind, and they called me between 7 PM and 8 PM the day before installation. They kept their appointments well, and most importantly, they installed it meticulously and explained how to use it. They installed it with a microfiber cloth placed on the floor to prevent scratches or dents. We opted for a drilled installation; although it would have been possible to run the wires through the baseboard under the sink without drilling, they advised that we would need to drill into the drawers or similar areas to secure the wires. So, we drilled into the sink. Before purchasing, I measured the dimensions and secured a spot before ordering. I installed it away from the gas stove, and while it turned out to be larger than expected, I am satisfied. 2. Background of Purchase. With childbirth approaching, I debated whether to buy a U-Pang or a dedicated steam sterilizer for baby bottles, or to purchase a small dishwasher to use for a long time. Boiling water sterilization is recommended for newborn bottles for at least 100 days, so that was another concern. Ultimately, after much deliberation, I purchased a dishwasher and am using it well. Before buying, I compared it with a product from Brand L, and I chose this one because it is hygienic; the interior of the dishwasher, excluding the bottom section, is made of stainless steel. The upper interior of Brand L's dishwasher was not stainless steel! 3. The cycle and method used for washing bottles (see photo). Plus some TMI. First, I gathered all the bottles at once and ran about 8 of them. I kept the used bottles in a washing container filled with detergent. I ran the dishwasher about 1-2 times a day, pre-washing them before putting them in. Since I was also pumping for mixed feeding, the dishwashing was no joke. (Is it just breast milk?). Newborns produce a huge amount of bottles, so I put them in the dishwasher and ran it, and also did boiling water sterilization once a day. I heard that dishwasher sterilization involves rinsing and drying at a total temperature of 75 degrees, so since my baby was a newborn, I also regularly sterilized the bottles in boiling water at 100 degrees. I am doing this in parallel because my baby is not yet 100 days old. (After the baby was 80 days old, I used dishwasher-washed bottles up to twice, and for the third use, I sterilized the washed bottles in boiling water. After 100 days, I plan to increase the frequency to 1-2 times a week for boiling water sterilization.) I calculated the time it takes for the dishwasher to run and the bottles to air dry. I had 9 bottles (160-200ml capacity) on hand, and 3 of them were large Lansino bottles (240ml). When the amount of formula I prepared per feeding was around 165ml, I just used them together, so I used a total of 12 bottles. As the baby grew and the intervals between feedings increased to 5-6 times a day, I think I ended up washing the bottles every two days. In the beginning, when I used a lot of bottles, if the bottles weren't completely dry after the dishwasher run and I was in a hurry, I would run the dishwasher, pour boiling water from a formula kettle into the bottles and nipples to rinse them once, and then warm up formula or pumped breast milk to feed them. I used Spectra bottles at the postpartum care center, so to ensure my baby wouldn't have trouble adjusting to the nipples when we came home, I used Spectra bottles and a breast pump (for mixed feeding). I also used Lansinoh glass bottles. Glass bottles tend to dry quickly and get nice and warm. (I plan to switch to glass bottles when I upgrade the model.) I used Mother-K liquid dishwasher detergent. On days when I did a thorough pre-wash, I used the rapid mode (29 minutes) and added an extra rinse (available once). (I also frequently use the combination of rapid + high-temperature sterilization + powerful drying; it takes 71 minutes). After the wash cycle finished, I selected the bottle sterilization cycle (a function that does not add detergent). On days when I did a pre-wash almost as well as a full wash? I sometimes just ran the bottle sterilization cycle plus an extra rinse (53 minutes), and this cycle does not add detergent separately. So, if I had washed the bottles thoroughly in the sink, I would either run the bottle sterilization cycle instead of the boiling water sterilization cycle, or I would do a quick pre-wash, select a rapid or standard wash cycle to clean the bottles, and then run the sterilization cycle again once finished. When I was feeling lazy, I would run the standard cycle (68 minutes) and add the powerful drying cycle. Tip! If you select the drying mode, pause it briefly after the wash is finished, open the door to shake off the water from the bottles, nipples, and accessories in the basket, and then run the drying cycle; they will be much drier then. Once it finishes, open the door a little later to take them out, move them to a drying rack, and air dry them naturally for faster drying. I put nipples and consumables in a separate basket because they tend to fly around inside when running. Since they don't dry completely after the cycle, I transferred them to a drying rack to air dry before using them again. Advantages: High-temperature sterilization is possible (however, high-temperature sterilization cannot be selected for the bottle or drum sterilization cycles). You can wash all baby items inside (make sure to check if the cycle is dishwasher-safe before putting items in; otherwise, they will shrink). If you put dishes in and use the powerful drying function, they dry well (curved items might retain some moisture inside, but everything else dries well and feels nice and warm). The door opens automatically after the wash is finished (some models do not open automatically, but the Bespoke model does). It is suitable for washing dishes left over after a meal for two. It didn't hold that little. (Glass food containers, clean dishes, cutlery, etc. I sometimes sterilize items with hot water, but I tried putting them in the dishwasher after a pre-wash a few times and it was fine. I checked how much it actually holds). It seems like it will be useful for washing baby food dishes and things like that. After about 20 uses, an alarm automatically pops up on the dishwasher display saying that drum sterilization is needed, and it is hygienic because it has a drum sterilization function (some models do not display this). Once the dishwasher finishes, the liquid detergent dispenser opens automatically (some models do not open). The noise level is not loud by my standards. The dishwasher basket comes out easily as a whole, and there is no difficulty putting it back in (some models are difficult to clean the inside because they don't come out or fit together well). Downside: Nowadays, they don't provide paper manuals; I downloaded the manual via the single-page QR code provided. I think it might be a bit difficult for elderly people to familiarize themselves with how to use it. Also, before purchasing, I was debating between a model with a hot air drying function (DW30CB300C model) and the model I have now installed. I ended up buying this one. Sometimes I wish it had a function to dry things thoroughly. I do wonder if I should have bought a different model. (But I heard that other models are almost the same and don't dry things thoroughly). Still, since it has a drying function, dishes with wide surfaces are mostly dry. (PPSU bottles don't dry all the way through, so you need to move them to a separate drying rack.) In my experience, moisture stays inside the dishwasher for a long time. Even when I leave the door open, I have to leave it open for several days for the inside to dry completely. (If you use it every day, you might not mind; since I only run the baby's items these days and only use it once every two days, the moisture bothered me.) I don't think the large dishwasher I used before was like this, so maybe it's because this is a small one. Overall, I am satisfied with it. Additional review after the baby turned 100 days. First, I do boiling water sterilization once a week these days. Then, I roughly wash things and use the Standard + High Temperature Sterilization + Extra Rinse + Power Dry (takes 1 hour and 41 minutes) cycle the most. I hardly use the separate bottle sterilization course anymore. I run it for everything related to the baby, such as bottles, teething toys, and pacifiers. I run the dishwasher once every 2 to 3 days. (Feeding intervals are 4 hours, using 4 bottles a day). When the dishwasher starts and there are 30 minutes left, it is the "Power Dry" time. It doesn't blow hot air or a breeze; instead, it works like a hair dryer. The principle is that water at a high temperature of over 70 degrees is sprayed, and that heat is transferred to the dishes to dry them. Dishes, plates, and glass, which retain thermal energy well, dry quickly, but plastics do not. (I checked the post on the Samsung Electronics website asking how to dry them well). I stop the dishwasher when there are 10 to 15 minutes left on the Power Dry timer. When I open the door, a lot of hot steam comes out. I organize the nipples, accessories, and bottles inside (shake off the water), put them back in properly, and press start. Once it is finished, the dishwasher door opens, and I move the items to the bottle drying rack to air dry. I wanted to share this in case anyone thought Power Dry just blows out air. No matter how much I think about it, I feel like I made the right purchase for my needs! Good luck with parenting! April 7, 2025 [Updated Review] The baby is over 172 days old (approaching 6 months). I have uploaded additional photos. I am reverently preparing and practicing solid foods. Why are there so many containers and tools? It is very, very good. I really think I made a great purchase! Bottles, teething toys, pacifiers, silicone medicine bottles, and even sucking toys made of dishwasher-safe materials—I put everything in there to wash and sterilize it. I am satisfied! Comments (English): [ I bought this to use exclusively for the baby, such as baby bottles, after giving birth. ] || ---------------- || This is a review written after using the product for about three months since its installation on October 9th. I purchased this before my baby was born to sterilize baby bottles and use it exclusively for baby-related items. I intend to run it exclusively for baby-related tasks. I have run it with baby bottles and clean, contaminated glass plates or bowls. Going forward, this dishwasher will handle the washing up that will come with introducing solid foods. Regarding after-sales service and estimated product lifespan: The product warranty is 1 year, the parts retention period is 5 years, and two core motor components are covered by warranties of 3 and 10 years. I chose this dishwasher with the intention of using it for about 4 to 5 years, and I am satisfied with both the price and performance. Since it is a new model and the parts retention period is up to 5 years, I decided to consider that to be a significant amount of use. 1. Installation: All the installation technicians were kind, and they called me between 7 PM and 8 PM the day before installation. They kept their appointments well, and most importantly, they installed it meticulously and explained how to use it. They installed it with a microfiber cloth placed on the floor to prevent scratches or dents. We opted for a drilled installation; although it would have been possible to run the wires through the baseboard under the sink without drilling, they advised that we would need to drill into the drawers or similar areas to secure the wires. So, we drilled into the sink. Before purchasing, I measured the dimensions and secured a spot before ordering. I installed it away from the gas stove, and while it turned out to be larger than expected, I am satisfied. 2. Background of Purchase. With childbirth approaching, I debated whether to buy a U-Pang or a dedicated steam sterilizer for baby bottles, or to purchase a small dishwasher to use for a long time. Boiling water sterilization is recommended for newborn bottles for at least 100 days, so that was another concern. Ultimately, after much deliberation, I purchased a dishwasher and am using it well. Before buying, I compared it with a product from Brand L, and I chose this one because it is hygienic; the interior of the dishwasher, excluding the bottom section, is made of stainless steel. The upper interior of Brand L's dishwasher was not stainless steel! 3. The cycle and method used for washing bottles (see photo). Plus some TMI. First, I gathered all the bottles at once and ran about 8 of them. I kept the used bottles in a washing container filled with detergent. I ran the dishwasher about 1-2 times a day, pre-washing them before putting them in. Since I was also pumping for mixed feeding, the dishwashing was no joke. (Is it just breast milk?). Newborns produce a huge amount of bottles, so I put them in the dishwasher and ran it, and also did boiling water sterilization once a day. I heard that dishwasher sterilization involves rinsing and drying at a total temperature of 75 degrees, so since my baby was a newborn, I also regularly sterilized the bottles in boiling water at 100 degrees. I am doing this in parallel because my baby is not yet 100 days old. (After the baby was 80 days old, I used dishwasher-washed bottles up to twice, and for the third use, I sterilized the washed bottles in boiling water. After 100 days, I plan to increase the frequency to 1-2 times a week for boiling water sterilization.) I calculated the time it takes for the dishwasher to run and the bottles to air dry. I had 9 bottles (160-200ml capacity) on hand, and 3 of them were large Lansino bottles (240ml). When the amount of formula I prepared per feeding was around 165ml, I just used them together, so I used a total of 12 bottles. As the baby grew and the intervals between feedings increased to 5-6 times a day, I think I ended up washing the bottles every two days. In the beginning, when I used a lot of bottles, if the bottles weren't completely dry after the dishwasher run and I was in a hurry, I would run the dishwasher, pour boiling water from a formula kettle into the bottles and nipples to rinse them once, and then warm up formula or pumped breast milk to feed them. I used Spectra bottles at the postpartum care center, so to ensure my baby wouldn't have trouble adjusting to the nipples when we came home, I used Spectra bottles and a breast pump (for mixed feeding). I also used Lansinoh glass bottles. Glass bottles tend to dry quickly and get nice and warm. (I plan to switch to glass bottles when I upgrade the model.) I used Mother-K liquid dishwasher detergent. On days when I did a thorough pre-wash, I used the rapid mode (29 minutes) and added an extra rinse (available once). (I also frequently use the combination of rapid + high-temperature sterilization + powerful drying; it takes 71 minutes). Comments (English): [ I bought this to use exclusively for the baby, such as baby bottles, after giving birth. ] || ---------------- || This is a review written after using the product for about three months since its installation on October 9th. I purchased this before my baby was born to sterilize baby bottles and use it exclusively for baby-related items. I intend to run it exclusively for baby-related tasks. I have run it with baby bottles and clean, contaminated glass plates or bowls. Going forward, this dishwasher will handle the washing up that will come with introducing solid foods. Regarding after-sales service and estimated product lifespan: The product warranty is 1 year, the parts retention period is 5 years, and two core motor components are covered by warranties of 3 and 10 years. I chose this dishwasher with the intention of using it for about 4 to 5 years, and I am satisfied with both the price and performance. Since it is a new model and the parts retention period is up to 5 years, I decided to consider that to be a significant amount of use. 1. Installation: All the installation technicians were kind, and they called me between 7 PM and 8 PM the day before installation. They kept their appointments well, and most importantly, they installed it meticulously and explained how to use it. They installed it with a microfiber cloth placed on the floor to prevent scratches or dents. We opted for a drilled installation; although it would have been possible to run the wires through the baseboard under the sink without drilling, they advised that we would need to drill into the drawers or similar areas to secure the wires. So, we drilled into the sink. Before purchasing, I measured the dimensions and secured a spot before ordering. I installed it away from the gas stove, and while it turned out to be larger than expected, I am satisfied. 2. Background of Purchase. With childbirth approaching, I debated whether to buy a U-Pang or a dedicated steam sterilizer for baby bottles, or to purchase a small dishwasher to use for a long time. Boiling water sterilization is recommended for newborn bottles for at least 100 days, so that was another concern. Ultimately, after much deliberation, I purchased a dishwasher and am using it well. Before buying, I compared it with a product from Brand L, and I chose this one because it is hygienic; the interior of the dishwasher, excluding the bottom section, is made of stainless steel. The upper interior of Brand L's dishwasher was not stainless steel! 3. The cycle and method used for washing bottles (see photo). Plus some TMI. First, I gathered all the bottles at once and ran about 8 of them. I kept the used bottles in a washing container filled with detergent. I ran the dishwasher about 1-2 times a day, pre-washing them before putting them in. Since I was also pumping for mixed feeding, the dishwashing was no joke. (Is it just breast milk?). Newborns produce a huge amount of bottles, so I put them in the dishwasher and ran it, and also did boiling water sterilization once a day. I heard that dishwasher sterilization involves rinsing and drying at a total temperature of 75 degrees, so since my baby was a newborn, I also regularly sterilized the bottles in boiling water at 100 degrees. I am doing this in parallel because my baby is not yet 100 days old. (After the baby was 80 days old, I used dishwasher-washed bottles up to twice, and for the third use, I sterilized the washed bottles in boiling water. After 100 days, I plan to increase the frequency to 1-2 times a week for boiling water sterilization.) I calculated the time it takes for the dishwasher to run and the bottles to air dry. I had 9 bottles (160-200ml capacity) on hand, and 3 of them were large Lansino bottles (240ml). When the amount of formula I prepared per feeding was around 165ml, I just used them together, so I used a total of 12 bottles. As the baby grew and the intervals between feedings increased to 5-6 times a day, I think I ended up washing the bottles every two days. In the beginning, when I used a lot of bottles, if the bottles weren't completely dry after the dishwasher run and I was in a hurry, I would run the dishwasher, pour boiling water from a formula kettle into the bottles and nipples to rinse them once, and then warm up formula or pumped breast milk to feed them. I used Spectra bottles at the postpartum care center, so to ensure my baby wouldn't have trouble adjusting to the nipples when we came home, I used Spectra bottles and a breast pump (for mixed feeding). I also used Lansinoh glass bottles. Glass bottles tend to dry quickly and get nice and warm. (I plan to switch to glass bottles when I upgrade the model.) I used Mother-K liquid dishwasher detergent. On days when I did a thorough pre-wash, I used the rapid mode (29 minutes) and added an extra rinse (available once). (I also frequently use the combination of rapid + high-temperature sterilization + powerful drying; it takes 71 minutes). After the wash cycle finished, I selected the bottle sterilization cycle (a function that does not add detergent). On days when I did a pre-wash almost as well as a full wash? I sometimes just ran the bottle sterilization cycle plus an extra rinse (53 minutes), and this cycle does not add detergent separately. So, if I had washed the bottles thoroughly in the sink, I would either run the bottle sterilization cycle instead of the boiling water sterilization cycle, or I would do a quick pre-wash, select a rapid or standard wash cycle to clean the bottles, and then run the sterilization cycle again once finished. When I was feeling lazy, I would run the standard cycle (68 minutes) and add the powerful drying cycle. Tip! If you select the drying mode, pause it briefly after the wash is finished, open the door to shake off the water from the bottles, nipples, and accessories in the basket, and then run the drying cycle; they will be much drier then. Once it finishes, open the door a little later to take them out, move them to a drying rack, and air dry them naturally for faster drying. I put nipples and consumables in a separate basket because they tend to fly around inside when running. Since they don't dry completely after the cycle, I transferred them to a drying rack to air dry before using them again. Advantages: High-temperature sterilization is possible (however, high-temperature sterilization cannot be selected for the bottle or drum sterilization cycles). You can wash all baby items inside (make sure to check if the cycle is dishwasher-safe before putting items in; otherwise, they will shrink). If you put dishes in and use the powerful drying function, they dry well (curved items might retain some moisture inside, but everything else dries well and feels nice and warm). The door opens automatically after the wash is finished (some models do not open automatically, but the Bespoke model does). It is suitable for washing dishes left over after a meal for two. It didn't hold that little. (Glass food containers, clean dishes, cutlery, etc. I sometimes sterilize items with hot water, but I tried putting them in the dishwasher after a pre-wash a few times and it was fine. I checked how much it actually holds). It seems like it will be useful for washing baby food dishes and things like that. After about 20 uses, an alarm automatically pops up on the dishwasher display saying that drum sterilization is needed, and it is hygienic because it has a drum sterilization function (some models do not display this). Once the dishwasher finishes, the liquid detergent dispenser opens automatically (some models do not open). The noise level is not loud by my standards. The dishwasher basket comes out easily as a whole, and there is no difficulty putting it back in (some models are difficult to clean the inside because they don't come out or fit together well). Downside: Nowadays, they don't provide paper manuals; I downloaded the manual via the single-page QR code provided. I think it might be a bit difficult for elderly people to familiarize themselves with how to use it. Also, before purchasing, I was debating between a model with a hot air drying function (DW30CB300C model) and the model I have now installed. I ended up buying this one. Sometimes I wish it had a function to dry things thoroughly. I do wonder if I should have bought a different model. (But I heard that other models are almost the same and don't dry things thoroughly). Still, since it has a drying function, dishes with wide surfaces are mostly dry. (PPSU bottles don't dry all the way through, so you need to move them to a separate drying rack.) In my experience, moisture stays inside the dishwasher for a long time. Even when I leave the door open, I have to leave it open for several days for the inside to dry completely. (If you use it every day, you might not mind; since I only run the baby's items these days and only use it once every two days, the moisture bothered me.) I don't think the large dishwasher I used before was like this, so maybe it's because this is a small one. Overall, I am satisfied with it. Additional review after the baby turned 100 days. First, I do boiling water sterilization once a week these days. Then, I roughly wash things and use the Standard + High Temperature Sterilization + Extra Rinse + Power Dry (takes 1 hour and 41 minutes) cycle the most. I hardly use the separate bottle sterilization course anymore. I run it for everything related to the baby, such as bottles, teething toys, and pacifiers. I run the dishwasher once every 2 to 3 days. (Feeding intervals are 4 hours, using 4 bottles a day). When the dishwasher starts and there are 30 minutes left, it is the "Power Dry" time. It doesn't blow hot air or a breeze; instead, it works like a hair dryer. The principle is that water at a high temperature of over 70 degrees is sprayed, and that heat is transferred to the dishes to dry them. Dishes, plates, and glass, which retain thermal energy well, dry quickly, but plastics do not. (I checked the post on the Samsung Electronics website asking how to dry them well). I stop the dishwasher when there are 10 to 15 minutes left on the Power Dry timer. When I open the door, a lot of hot steam comes out. I organize the nipples, accessories, and bottles inside (shake off the water), put them back in properly, and press start. Once it is finished, the dishwasher door opens, and I move the items to the bottle drying rack to air dry. I wanted to share this in case anyone thought Power Dry just blows out air. No matter how much I think about it, I feel like I made the right purchase for my needs! Good luck with parenting! April 7, 2025 [Updated Review] The baby is over 172 days old (approaching 6 months). I have uploaded additional photos. I am reverently preparing and practicing solid foods. Why are there so many containers and tools? It is very, very good. I really think I made a great purchase! Bottles, teething toys, pacifiers, silicone medicine bottles, and even sucking toys made of dishwasher-safe materials—I put everything in there to wash and sterilize it. I am satisfied! If my honest review of a product I bought with my own money was helpful, please press the like button~
