(수유텀 4시간, 젖병 1일 4병 사용함)식세기 돌아가고 마지막 30분 남았을때 강력건조 시간인데건조 열풍이나 바람이 나오는게 아니고, 드라이기 말리는 형식으로, 고온 70도 이상물이 뿌려지고 그 열기가 식기로 전달되어 건조되는 원리랍니다. 열에너지를 잘가지고 있는 그릇 접시 유리들은 빨리건조되고, 플라스틱 들은 그렇치 못해요ㅜ.ㅜ .(삼성전자 사이트에서 건조가 잘되는법을 알려주세요 글 확인함)강력건조한 건조시간 10~15분 남았을때 정지 후. 문열면 뜨거운 김, 수증기가 많이 나와요. 안에 젖꼭지 부속품들 젖병 등 정리(물기털기)를 하고 다시 바르게 넣코 시작 누른 뒤. 다 끝나면 식세기 문이 열리고, 젖병건조대로 옮겨서 자연건조 시키고 있어용.혹시 강력건조가 바람나온다고 생각하실까봐 공유드리구요.계속 생각해도 목적에 맞게 잘산거 같아요!육아 홧팅입니다!✅️ 25년 4월 7일 추가후기 아기는 생후 172일 넘음 (6개월 되어감) 추가사진 업로드함.이유식을 경건하게 준비 및 연습하는데.. 이유식 용기들 도구들 왜케 많이나오죠.. 매우 매우 좋습니다. 진짜 잘산거 같아요!젖병들도 치발기 쪽쪽이 실리콘약병.. 식세기 넣어도 되는 소재의 빠는 장난감들.. 모두모두 잘 넣어서 씻고 살균합니다. 만족합니다! 저의 내돈내산 솔찍 리뷰가 도움 되셨다면 좋아요 꾸욱 눌러주세요~❤️

Sentence (English): No matter how much I think about it, I feel like I made the right purchase for my needs!
Comments (English): [ I bought this to use exclusively for the baby, such as baby bottles, after giving birth. ] || ---------------- || This is a review written after using the product for about three months since its installation on October 9th. I purchased this before my baby was born to sterilize baby bottles and use it exclusively for baby-related items. I intend to run it exclusively for baby-related tasks. I have run it with baby bottles and clean, contaminated glass plates or bowls. Going forward, this dishwasher will handle the washing up that will come with introducing solid foods. Regarding after-sales service and estimated product lifespan: The product warranty is 1 year, the parts retention period is 5 years, and two core motor components are covered by warranties of 3 and 10 years. I chose this dishwasher with the intention of using it for about 4 to 5 years, and I am satisfied with both the price and performance. Since it is a new model and the parts retention period is up to 5 years, I decided to consider that to be a significant amount of use. 1. Installation: All the installation technicians were kind, and they called me between 7 PM and 8 PM the day before installation. They kept their appointments well, and most importantly, they installed it meticulously and explained how to use it. They installed it with a microfiber cloth placed on the floor to prevent scratches or dents. We opted for a drilled installation; although it would have been possible to run the wires through the baseboard under the sink without drilling, they advised that we would need to drill into the drawers or similar areas to secure the wires. So, we drilled into the sink. Before purchasing, I measured the dimensions and secured a spot before ordering. I installed it away from the gas stove, and while it turned out to be larger than expected, I am satisfied. 2. Background of Purchase. With childbirth approaching, I debated whether to buy a U-Pang or a dedicated steam sterilizer for baby bottles, or to purchase a small dishwasher to use for a long time. Boiling water sterilization is recommended for newborn bottles for at least 100 days, so that was another concern. Ultimately, after much deliberation, I purchased a dishwasher and am using it well. Before buying, I compared it with a product from Brand L, and I chose this one because it is hygienic; the interior of the dishwasher, excluding the bottom section, is made of stainless steel. The upper interior of Brand L's dishwasher was not stainless steel! 3. The cycle and method used for washing bottles (see photo). Plus some TMI. First, I gathered all the bottles at once and ran about 8 of them. I kept the used bottles in a washing container filled with detergent. I ran the dishwasher about 1-2 times a day, pre-washing them before putting them in. Since I was also pumping for mixed feeding, the dishwashing was no joke. (Is it just breast milk?). Newborns produce a huge amount of bottles, so I put them in the dishwasher and ran it, and also did boiling water sterilization once a day. I heard that dishwasher sterilization involves rinsing and drying at a total temperature of 75 degrees, so since my baby was a newborn, I also regularly sterilized the bottles in boiling water at 100 degrees. I am doing this in parallel because my baby is not yet 100 days old. (After the baby was 80 days old, I used dishwasher-washed bottles up to twice, and for the third use, I sterilized the washed bottles in boiling water. After 100 days, I plan to increase the frequency to 1-2 times a week for boiling water sterilization.) I calculated the time it takes for the dishwasher to run and the bottles to air dry. I had 9 bottles (160-200ml capacity) on hand, and 3 of them were large Lansino bottles (240ml). When the amount of formula I prepared per feeding was around 165ml, I just used them together, so I used a total of 12 bottles. As the baby grew and the intervals between feedings increased to 5-6 times a day, I think I ended up washing the bottles every two days. In the beginning, when I used a lot of bottles, if the bottles weren't completely dry after the dishwasher run and I was in a hurry, I would run the dishwasher, pour boiling water from a formula kettle into the bottles and nipples to rinse them once, and then warm up formula or pumped breast milk to feed them. I used Spectra bottles at the postpartum care center, so to ensure my baby wouldn't have trouble adjusting to the nipples when we came home, I used Spectra bottles and a breast pump (for mixed feeding). I also used Lansinoh glass bottles. Glass bottles tend to dry quickly and get nice and warm. (I plan to switch to glass bottles when I upgrade the model.) I used Mother-K liquid dishwasher detergent. On days when I did a thorough pre-wash, I used the rapid mode (29 minutes) and added an extra rinse (available once). (I also frequently use the combination of rapid + high-temperature sterilization + powerful drying; it takes 71 minutes). After the wash cycle finished, I selected the bottle sterilization cycle (a function that does not add detergent). On days when I did a pre-wash almost as well as a full wash? I sometimes just ran the bottle sterilization cycle plus an extra rinse (53 minutes), and this cycle does not add detergent separately. Comments (English): [ I bought this to use exclusively for the baby, such as baby bottles, after giving birth. ] || ---------------- || This is a review written after using the product for about three months since its installation on October 9th. I purchased this before my baby was born to sterilize baby bottles and use it exclusively for baby-related items. I intend to run it exclusively for baby-related tasks. I have run it with baby bottles and clean, contaminated glass plates or bowls. Going forward, this dishwasher will handle the washing up that will come with introducing solid foods. Regarding after-sales service and estimated product lifespan: The product warranty is 1 year, the parts retention period is 5 years, and two core motor components are covered by warranties of 3 and 10 years. I chose this dishwasher with the intention of using it for about 4 to 5 years, and I am satisfied with both the price and performance. Since it is a new model and the parts retention period is up to 5 years, I decided to consider that to be a significant amount of use. 1. Installation: All the installation technicians were kind, and they called me between 7 PM and 8 PM the day before installation. They kept their appointments well, and most importantly, they installed it meticulously and explained how to use it. They installed it with a microfiber cloth placed on the floor to prevent scratches or dents. We opted for a drilled installation; although it would have been possible to run the wires through the baseboard under the sink without drilling, they advised that we would need to drill into the drawers or similar areas to secure the wires. So, we drilled into the sink. Before purchasing, I measured the dimensions and secured a spot before ordering. I installed it away from the gas stove, and while it turned out to be larger than expected, I am satisfied. 2. Background of Purchase. With childbirth approaching, I debated whether to buy a U-Pang or a dedicated steam sterilizer for baby bottles, or to purchase a small dishwasher to use for a long time. Boiling water sterilization is recommended for newborn bottles for at least 100 days, so that was another concern. Ultimately, after much deliberation, I purchased a dishwasher and am using it well. Before buying, I compared it with a product from Brand L, and I chose this one because it is hygienic; the interior of the dishwasher, excluding the bottom section, is made of stainless steel. The upper interior of Brand L's dishwasher was not stainless steel! 3. The cycle and method used for washing bottles (see photo). Plus some TMI. First, I gathered all the bottles at once and ran about 8 of them. I kept the used bottles in a washing container filled with detergent. I ran the dishwasher about 1-2 times a day, pre-washing them before putting them in. Since I was also pumping for mixed feeding, the dishwashing was no joke. (Is it just breast milk?). Newborns produce a huge amount of bottles, so I put them in the dishwasher and ran it, and also did boiling water sterilization once a day. I heard that dishwasher sterilization involves rinsing and drying at a total temperature of 75 degrees, so since my baby was a newborn, I also regularly sterilized the bottles in boiling water at 100 degrees. I am doing this in parallel because my baby is not yet 100 days old. (After the baby was 80 days old, I used dishwasher-washed bottles up to twice, and for the third use, I sterilized the washed bottles in boiling water. After 100 days, I plan to increase the frequency to 1-2 times a week for boiling water sterilization.) I calculated the time it takes for the dishwasher to run and the bottles to air dry. I had 9 bottles (160-200ml capacity) on hand, and 3 of them were large Lansino bottles (240ml). When the amount of formula I prepared per feeding was around 165ml, I just used them together, so I used a total of 12 bottles. As the baby grew and the intervals between feedings increased to 5-6 times a day, I think I ended up washing the bottles every two days. In the beginning, when I used a lot of bottles, if the bottles weren't completely dry after the dishwasher run and I was in a hurry, I would run the dishwasher, pour boiling water from a formula kettle into the bottles and nipples to rinse them once, and then warm up formula or pumped breast milk to feed them. I used Spectra bottles at the postpartum care center, so to ensure my baby wouldn't have trouble adjusting to the nipples when we came home, I used Spectra bottles and a breast pump (for mixed feeding). I also used Lansinoh glass bottles. Glass bottles tend to dry quickly and get nice and warm. (I plan to switch to glass bottles when I upgrade the model.) I used Mother-K liquid dishwasher detergent. On days when I did a thorough pre-wash, I used the rapid mode (29 minutes) and added an extra rinse (available once). (I also frequently use the combination of rapid + high-temperature sterilization + powerful drying; it takes 71 minutes). After the wash cycle finished, I selected the bottle sterilization cycle (a function that does not add detergent). On days when I did a pre-wash almost as well as a full wash? I sometimes just ran the bottle sterilization cycle plus an extra rinse (53 minutes), and this cycle does not add detergent separately. So, if I had washed the bottles thoroughly in the sink, I would either run the bottle sterilization cycle instead of the boiling water sterilization cycle, or I would do a quick pre-wash, select a rapid or standard wash cycle to clean the bottles, and then run the sterilization cycle again once finished. When I was feeling lazy, I would run the standard cycle (68 minutes) and add the powerful drying cycle. Tip! If you select the drying mode, pause it briefly after the wash is finished, open the door to shake off the water from the bottles, nipples, and accessories in the basket, and then run the drying cycle; they will be much drier then. Once it finishes, open the door a little later to take them out, move them to a drying rack, and air dry them naturally for faster drying. I put nipples and consumables in a separate basket because they tend to fly around inside when running. Since they don't dry completely after the cycle, I transferred them to a drying rack to air dry before using them again. Advantages: High-temperature sterilization is possible (however, high-temperature sterilization cannot be selected for the bottle or drum sterilization cycles). You can wash all baby items inside (make sure to check if the cycle is dishwasher-safe before putting items in; otherwise, they will shrink). If you put dishes in and use the powerful drying function, they dry well (curved items might retain some moisture inside, but everything else dries well and feels nice and warm). The door opens automatically after the wash is finished (some models do not open automatically, but the Bespoke model does). It is suitable for washing dishes left over after a meal for two. It didn't hold that little. (Glass food containers, clean dishes, cutlery, etc. I sometimes sterilize items with hot water, but I tried putting them in the dishwasher after a pre-wash a few times and it was fine. I checked how much it actually holds). It seems like it will be useful for washing baby food dishes and things like that. After about 20 uses, an alarm automatically pops up on the dishwasher display saying that drum sterilization is needed, and it is hygienic because it has a drum sterilization function (some models do not display this). Once the dishwasher finishes, the liquid detergent dispenser opens automatically (some models do not open). The noise level is not loud by my standards. The dishwasher basket comes out easily as a whole, and there is no difficulty putting it back in (some models are difficult to clean the inside because they don't come out or fit together well). Downside: Nowadays, they don't provide paper manuals; I downloaded the manual via the single-page QR code provided. I think it might be a bit difficult for elderly people to familiarize themselves with how to use it. Also, before purchasing, I was debating between a model with a hot air drying function (DW30CB300C model) and the model I have now installed. I ended up buying this one. Sometimes I wish it had a function to dry things thoroughly. I do wonder if I should have bought a different model. (But I heard that other models are almost the same and don't dry things thoroughly). Still, since it has a drying function, dishes with wide surfaces are mostly dry. (PPSU bottles don't dry all the way through, so you need to move them to a separate drying rack.) In my experience, moisture stays inside the dishwasher for a long time. Even when I leave the door open, I have to leave it open for several days for the inside to dry completely. (If you use it every day, you might not mind; since I only run the baby's items these days and only use it once every two days, the moisture bothered me.) I don't think the large dishwasher I used before was like this, so maybe it's because this is a small one. Overall, I am satisfied with it. Additional review after the baby turned 100 days. First, I do boiling water sterilization once a week these days. Then, I roughly wash things and use the Standard + High Temperature Sterilization + Extra Rinse + Power Dry (takes 1 hour and 41 minutes) cycle the most. I hardly use the separate bottle sterilization course anymore. I run it for everything related to the baby, such as bottles, teething toys, and pacifiers. I run the dishwasher once every 2 to 3 days. (Feeding intervals are 4 hours, using 4 bottles a day). When the dishwasher starts and there are 30 minutes left, it is the "Power Dry" time. It doesn't blow hot air or a breeze; instead, it works like a hair dryer. The principle is that water at a high temperature of over 70 degrees is sprayed, and that heat is transferred to the dishes to dry them. Dishes, plates, and glass, which retain thermal energy well, dry quickly, but plastics do not. (I checked the post on the Samsung Electronics website asking how to dry them well). I stop the dishwasher when there are 10 to 15 minutes left on the Power Dry timer. When I open the door, a lot of hot steam comes out. I organize the nipples, accessories, and bottles inside (shake off the water), put them back in properly, and press start. Once it is finished, the dishwasher door opens, and I move the items to the bottle drying rack to air dry. I wanted to share this in case anyone thought Power Dry just blows out air. No matter how much I think about it, I feel like I made the right purchase for my needs! Good luck with parenting! April 7, 2025 [Updated Review] The baby is over 172 days old (approaching 6 months). I have uploaded additional photos. I am reverently preparing and practicing solid foods. Why are there so many containers and tools? It is very, very good. I really think I made a great purchase! Bottles, teething toys, pacifiers, silicone medicine bottles, and even sucking toys made of dishwasher-safe materials—I put everything in there to wash and sterilize it. I am satisfied! If my honest review of a product I bought with my own money was helpful, please press the like button~

(생후 80일 지나고 부턴 2번까지 젖병 식세기 돌린걸로 쓰고, 3번째 쓸때는 세척된 젖병들 열탕소독 함, 100일 지나면 주 1~2회 정도로 텀 늘려서 열탕소독 예정)식세기 돌아가고 자연건조 되는 시간. 고려해서 돌렸었구요. 젖병 9개(160~200ml용량) 구비했고, 3개는 란시노 큰거(240ml)인데 1회 분유타는 량이 165ml 정도로 되었을땐 걍 같이 써서 젖병 총 12개 사용했습니다. 애기가 커서 하루 5~6번 수유로 텀이 늘다보니 2일에 1번으로 젖병 세척돌리게 된거 같아요.초반에 젖병 많이 쓸때는.. 식세기 돌리고 젖병 건조가 덜되서 급할땐 식세기 돌아가고 분유포트 끓인물 젖병이랑 젖꼭지에 넣코 한번 헹구고 분유나 유축모유 데워서 줬어요.저는 조리원에서 스펙트라 젖병을 써서 아기 집에왔을때 젖꼭지 적응 힘들지 말라고 스펙트라 젖병이랑 유축기(혼합수유함) 썼어요.그리고 같이 란시노 유리젖병도 썼습니다.  유리젖병은 빨리 마르는 편이고 뜨끈뜨끈 합니다. (단계업하면 다 유리젖병으로 교체예정)세제는 마더케이 액상식세기 세제 사용했습니다. 꼼꼼하게 애벌세척을 했던 날은, 급속모드(29분)를 사용하고 헹굼추가(1회 가능)를 했습니다. (급속+고온살균+강력건조 이 조합도 잘씀 71분 뜸)그리고 나서 세척 코스가 끝나면, 그 다음 젖병살균코스(세제투입 안되는 기능임)를 선택했어요. 애벌세척을 거의 세척급으로 잘한날은?그냥 젖병살균코스+헹굼추가(53분)만 돌리기도 했는데, 이 코스는 세제가 따로 투입되거나 하지 않아요.그래서 따로 싱크대에서 세척을 잘 했으면, 젖병살균 코스만 열탕소독 대신 개념으로 돌리던가, 아니면 애벌세척 대충하고, 급속이나 표준으로 세척코스를 선택해 젖병을 씻고, 끝나면 다시 살균코스를 돌리는 방법을 택했습니다.영 귀찮을땐, 표준(68분)으로 돌리고, 강력건조를 추가했어요. 팁!! 건조모드 선택하면 세척 끝나면 그때 잠시 정지 후 열고 젖병이랑 젖꼭지 부속품들 바스켓에 넣어둔거 물기 탈탈 털어주고 건조모드 돌리면 그나마 많이 말라있어요. 종료되면 문 좀 늦게 열고 꺼내서 젖병 건조대 이동 후 자연 건조시 빨리 마름.젖꼭지나 소모품은 돌리면 여기저기 내부에서 튀어다녀서 별도 바스켓에 넣어서 돌렸어요. 다 돌아가고 나면 뽀송하게 바싹 안마르기 때문에 따로 건조대로 옮겨서 말려주고 사용했습니다. ✅️장점고온살균이 가능해요. (단 젖병살균 통살균 코스로는 고온살균이 선택이 안됩니다)아기 용품들 다 넣어서 세척이 가능해요(넣기전에 식세기 사용해도 되는 코스인지 꼭 확인하고 돌리세요. 안그러면서 쪼그라듭니다. )그릇 등 넣고 강력건조 기능쓰면 잘 말라요.(굴곡진 것들은 안에 물기가 좀 남아있고, 그 외에는 잘 말라있음 뜨끈뜨끈함)세척이 끝나고 자동으로 문이 열려요(일부 안열리는 모델들이 있음, 비스포크는 열림)2인 식사후 나오는 그릇 등 세척하기에 적합해요. 그렇케 조금 들어가지 않았어요. (유리 락앤락 반찬통들, 깨끗한 그릇들, 수저 식기류들 등.. 가끔 뜨거운물로 소독하는데, 애벌세척 후 식세기에 넣어서 몇번 써보니까 괜찮았어요. 얼마나 들어가나 봄)이유식 그릇 등 돌릴때 유용할꺼 같습니다. 20회 정도 사용하고 나면, 식세기 디스플레이에 자동으로 통살균 필요하다고 알람이 뜨고 통살균 기능이 있어서 위생적이에요.(안뜨는 기기들도 있음.)식세기 다 돌아가고 나면 액상 세제 투입기가 자동으로 열려있음 (안열리는 모델도 있음)소음이 내기준 크지 않음. 식세기 바스켓 통째로 잘빼지고 다시 끼는데 어려움 없음.( 잘 안빼지고 안껴져서 내부 청소하기 힘든 모델들이 있음..)✅️단점설명서가 요즘은 종이로 안줌, 주신 한장짜리 큐알 들어가서 설명서 다운받았어요. 어르신들이 사용법을 숙지하시기에는 좀 어려움이 있으실꺼 같습니다. 또 구매전에 열풍건조기능이 있는 제품(DW30CB300C모델)이랑 지금 설치한 모델이랑 고민을 했었는데.. 이거로 구매했고.가끔 바싹 말려주는 기능이 있으면 좋켔다.. 다른 모델로 샀으면 어땠을까? 생각이 들긴하더라구요. (근데 다른 모델도 거의 똑같데요 바싹 안말려준데요)그래도 건조기능이 있어서 표면이 넓은 그릇들은 거의 말라있긴 합니다. (ppsu 젖병은 속까지 안말라요.. 따로 건조대 이동 필요함)식세기 기기 내부에 물기가 내기준 오래 있어요. 문열고 있어도 몇일을 열어놔야 안이 바싹 마르더라구요... (매일 쓰면 신경 안쓸 수 있음, 요즘 애기꺼만 돌리다보니 2일에 1회 써서 물기들이 신경쓰였음) 이전에 쓰던 대형 식세기는 안그랬던거 같은데, 소형이라 그런가봐요;;전반적으로 만족하며 사용하고 있습니다.✅️ 아기 100일  지나고 추가후기우선 요즘 열탕소독을 주1회 합니다.그리고 대강 씻어서 표준+고온살균+헹굼추가+강력건조( 1시간 41분 뜸)를. 제일 많이 씁니다. 따로 젖병살균코스는 이제 거의 안쓰게 되네용. 젖병 치발기 쪽쪽이 애기에 대한거 다 돌립니다. 2~3일에 1번씩 식세기 돌려요. (수유텀 4시간, 젖병 1일 4병 사용함)식세기 돌아가고 마지막 30분 남았을때 강력건조 시간인데건조 열풍이나 바람이 나오는게 아니고, 드라이기 말리는 형식으로, 고온 70도 이상물이 뿌려지고 그 열기가 식기로 전달되어 건조되는 원리랍니다. 열에너지를 잘가지고 있는 그릇 접시 유리들은 빨리건조되고, 플라스틱 들은 그렇치 못해요ㅜ.ㅜ .(삼성전자 사이트에서 건조가 잘되는법을 알려주세요 글 확인함)강력건조한 건조시간 10~15분 남았을때 정지 후. 문열면 뜨거운 김, 수증기가 많이 나와요. 안에 젖꼭지 부속품들 젖병 등 정리(물기털기)를 하고 다시 바르게 넣코 시작 누른 뒤. 다 끝나면 식세기 문이 열리고, 젖병건조대로 옮겨서 자연건조 시키고 있어용.혹시 강력건조가 바람나온다고 생각하실까봐 공유드리구요.계속 생각해도 목적에 맞게 잘산거 같아요!육아 홧팅입니다!✅️ 25년 4월 7일 추가후기 아기는 생후 172일 넘음 (6개월 되어감) 추가사진 업로드함.이유식을 경건하게 준비 및 연습하는데.. 이유식 용기들 도구들 왜케 많이나오죠.. 매우 매우 좋습니다. 진짜 잘산거 같아요!젖병들도 치발기 쪽쪽이 실리콘약병.. 식세기 넣어도 되는 소재의 빠는 장난감들.. 모두모두 잘 넣어서 씻고 살균합니다. 만족합니다! 저의 내돈내산 솔찍 리뷰가 도움 되셨다면 좋아요 꾸욱 눌러주세요~❤️

Sentence (English): April 7, 2025 [Updated Review] The baby is over 172 days old (approaching 6 months).
Comments (English): [ I bought this to use exclusively for the baby, such as baby bottles, after giving birth. ] || ---------------- || This is a review written after using the product for about three months since its installation on October 9th. I purchased this before my baby was born to sterilize baby bottles and use it exclusively for baby-related items. I intend to run it exclusively for baby-related tasks. I have run it with baby bottles and clean, contaminated glass plates or bowls. Going forward, this dishwasher will handle the washing up that will come with introducing solid foods. Regarding after-sales service and estimated product lifespan: The product warranty is 1 year, the parts retention period is 5 years, and two core motor components are covered by warranties of 3 and 10 years. I chose this dishwasher with the intention of using it for about 4 to 5 years, and I am satisfied with both the price and performance. Since it is a new model and the parts retention period is up to 5 years, I decided to consider that to be a significant amount of use. 1. Installation: All the installation technicians were kind, and they called me between 7 PM and 8 PM the day before installation. They kept their appointments well, and most importantly, they installed it meticulously and explained how to use it. They installed it with a microfiber cloth placed on the floor to prevent scratches or dents. We opted for a drilled installation; although it would have been possible to run the wires through the baseboard under the sink without drilling, they advised that we would need to drill into the drawers or similar areas to secure the wires. So, we drilled into the sink. Before purchasing, I measured the dimensions and secured a spot before ordering. I installed it away from the gas stove, and while it turned out to be larger than expected, I am satisfied. 2. Background of Purchase. With childbirth approaching, I debated whether to buy a U-Pang or a dedicated steam sterilizer for baby bottles, or to purchase a small dishwasher to use for a long time. Boiling water sterilization is recommended for newborn bottles for at least 100 days, so that was another concern. Ultimately, after much deliberation, I purchased a dishwasher and am using it well. Before buying, I compared it with a product from Brand L, and I chose this one because it is hygienic; the interior of the dishwasher, excluding the bottom section, is made of stainless steel. The upper interior of Brand L's dishwasher was not stainless steel! 3. The cycle and method used for washing bottles (see photo). Plus some TMI. First, I gathered all the bottles at once and ran about 8 of them. I kept the used bottles in a washing container filled with detergent. I ran the dishwasher about 1-2 times a day, pre-washing them before putting them in. Since I was also pumping for mixed feeding, the dishwashing was no joke. (Is it just breast milk?). Newborns produce a huge amount of bottles, so I put them in the dishwasher and ran it, and also did boiling water sterilization once a day. I heard that dishwasher sterilization involves rinsing and drying at a total temperature of 75 degrees, so since my baby was a newborn, I also regularly sterilized the bottles in boiling water at 100 degrees. I am doing this in parallel because my baby is not yet 100 days old. (After the baby was 80 days old, I used dishwasher-washed bottles up to twice, and for the third use, I sterilized the washed bottles in boiling water. After 100 days, I plan to increase the frequency to 1-2 times a week for boiling water sterilization.) I calculated the time it takes for the dishwasher to run and the bottles to air dry. I had 9 bottles (160-200ml capacity) on hand, and 3 of them were large Lansino bottles (240ml). When the amount of formula I prepared per feeding was around 165ml, I just used them together, so I used a total of 12 bottles. As the baby grew and the intervals between feedings increased to 5-6 times a day, I think I ended up washing the bottles every two days. In the beginning, when I used a lot of bottles, if the bottles weren't completely dry after the dishwasher run and I was in a hurry, I would run the dishwasher, pour boiling water from a formula kettle into the bottles and nipples to rinse them once, and then warm up formula or pumped breast milk to feed them. I used Spectra bottles at the postpartum care center, so to ensure my baby wouldn't have trouble adjusting to the nipples when we came home, I used Spectra bottles and a breast pump (for mixed feeding). I also used Lansinoh glass bottles. Glass bottles tend to dry quickly and get nice and warm. (I plan to switch to glass bottles when I upgrade the model.) I used Mother-K liquid dishwasher detergent. On days when I did a thorough pre-wash, I used the rapid mode (29 minutes) and added an extra rinse (available once). (I also frequently use the combination of rapid + high-temperature sterilization + powerful drying; it takes 71 minutes). After the wash cycle finished, I selected the bottle sterilization cycle (a function that does not add detergent). On days when I did a pre-wash almost as well as a full wash? I sometimes just ran the bottle sterilization cycle plus an extra rinse (53 minutes), and this cycle does not add detergent separately. So, if I had washed the bottles thoroughly in the sink, I would either run the bottle sterilization cycle instead of the boiling water sterilization cycle, or I would do a quick pre-wash, select a rapid or standard wash cycle to clean the bottles, and then run the sterilization cycle again once finished. When I was feeling lazy, I would run the standard cycle (68 minutes) and add the powerful drying cycle. Tip! If you select the drying mode, pause it briefly after the wash is finished, open the door to shake off the water from the bottles, nipples, and accessories in the basket, and then run the drying cycle; they will be much drier then. Once it finishes, open the door a little later to take them out, move them to a drying rack, and air dry them naturally for faster drying. I put nipples and consumables in a separate basket because they tend to fly around inside when running. Since they don't dry completely after the cycle, I transferred them to a drying rack to air dry before using them again. Advantages: High-temperature sterilization is possible (however, high-temperature sterilization cannot be selected for the bottle or drum sterilization cycles). You can wash all baby items inside (make sure to check if the cycle is dishwasher-safe before putting items in; otherwise, they will shrink). If you put dishes in and use the powerful drying function, they dry well (curved items might retain some moisture inside, but everything else dries well and feels nice and warm). The door opens automatically after the wash is finished (some models do not open automatically, but the Bespoke model does). It is suitable for washing dishes left over after a meal for two. It didn't hold that little. (Glass food containers, clean dishes, cutlery, etc. I sometimes sterilize items with hot water, but I tried putting them in the dishwasher after a pre-wash a few times and it was fine. I checked how much it actually holds). It seems like it will be useful for washing baby food dishes and things like that. After about 20 uses, an alarm automatically pops up on the dishwasher display saying that drum sterilization is needed, and it is hygienic because it has a drum sterilization function (some models do not display this). Once the dishwasher finishes, the liquid detergent dispenser opens automatically (some models do not open). The noise level is not loud by my standards. The dishwasher basket comes out easily as a whole, and there is no difficulty putting it back in (some models are difficult to clean the inside because they don't come out or fit together well). Downside: Nowadays, they don't provide paper manuals; I downloaded the manual via the single-page QR code provided. I think it might be a bit difficult for elderly people to familiarize themselves with how to use it. Also, before purchasing, I was debating between a model with a hot air drying function (DW30CB300C model) and the model I have now installed. I ended up buying this one. Sometimes I wish it had a function to dry things thoroughly. I do wonder if I should have bought a different model. (But I heard that other models are almost the same and don't dry things thoroughly). Still, since it has a drying function, dishes with wide surfaces are mostly dry. (PPSU bottles don't dry all the way through, so you need to move them to a separate drying rack.) In my experience, moisture stays inside the dishwasher for a long time. Even when I leave the door open, I have to leave it open for several days for the inside to dry completely. (If you use it every day, you might not mind; since I only run the baby's items these days and only use it once every two days, the moisture bothered me.) I don't think the large dishwasher I used before was like this, so maybe it's because this is a small one. Overall, I am satisfied with it. Additional review after the baby turned 100 days. First, I do boiling water sterilization once a week these days. Then, I roughly wash things and use the Standard + High Temperature Sterilization + Extra Rinse + Power Dry (takes 1 hour and 41 minutes) cycle the most. I hardly use the separate bottle sterilization course anymore. I run it for everything related to the baby, such as bottles, teething toys, and pacifiers. I run the dishwasher once every 2 to 3 days. (Feeding intervals are 4 hours, using 4 bottles a day). When the dishwasher starts and there are 30 minutes left, it is the "Power Dry" time. It doesn't blow hot air or a breeze; instead, it works like a hair dryer. The principle is that water at a high temperature of over 70 degrees is sprayed, and that heat is transferred to the dishes to dry them. Dishes, plates, and glass, which retain thermal energy well, dry quickly, but plastics do not. (I checked the post on the Samsung Electronics website asking how to dry them well). I stop the dishwasher when there are 10 to 15 minutes left on the Power Dry timer. When I open the door, a lot of hot steam comes out. I organize the nipples, accessories, and bottles inside (shake off the water), put them back in properly, and press start. Once it is finished, the dishwasher door opens, and I move the items to the bottle drying rack to air dry. I wanted to share this in case anyone thought Power Dry just blows out air. No matter how much I think about it, I feel like I made the right purchase for my needs! Good luck with parenting! April 7, 2025 [Updated Review] The baby is over 172 days old (approaching 6 months). I have uploaded additional photos. I am reverently preparing and practicing solid foods. Why are there so many containers and tools? It is very, very good. I really think I made a great purchase! Bottles, teething toys, pacifiers, silicone medicine bottles, and even sucking toys made of dishwasher-safe materials—I put everything in there to wash and sterilize it. I am satisfied! Comments (English): [ I bought this to use exclusively for the baby, such as baby bottles, after giving birth. ] || ---------------- || This is a review written after using the product for about three months since its installation on October 9th. I purchased this before my baby was born to sterilize baby bottles and use it exclusively for baby-related items. I intend to run it exclusively for baby-related tasks. I have run it with baby bottles and clean, contaminated glass plates or bowls. Going forward, this dishwasher will handle the washing up that will come with introducing solid foods. Regarding after-sales service and estimated product lifespan: The product warranty is 1 year, the parts retention period is 5 years, and two core motor components are covered by warranties of 3 and 10 years. I chose this dishwasher with the intention of using it for about 4 to 5 years, and I am satisfied with both the price and performance. Since it is a new model and the parts retention period is up to 5 years, I decided to consider that to be a significant amount of use. 1. Installation: All the installation technicians were kind, and they called me between 7 PM and 8 PM the day before installation. They kept their appointments well, and most importantly, they installed it meticulously and explained how to use it. They installed it with a microfiber cloth placed on the floor to prevent scratches or dents. We opted for a drilled installation; although it would have been possible to run the wires through the baseboard under the sink without drilling, they advised that we would need to drill into the drawers or similar areas to secure the wires. So, we drilled into the sink. Before purchasing, I measured the dimensions and secured a spot before ordering. I installed it away from the gas stove, and while it turned out to be larger than expected, I am satisfied. 2. Background of Purchase. With childbirth approaching, I debated whether to buy a U-Pang or a dedicated steam sterilizer for baby bottles, or to purchase a small dishwasher to use for a long time. Boiling water sterilization is recommended for newborn bottles for at least 100 days, so that was another concern. Ultimately, after much deliberation, I purchased a dishwasher and am using it well. Before buying, I compared it with a product from Brand L, and I chose this one because it is hygienic; the interior of the dishwasher, excluding the bottom section, is made of stainless steel. The upper interior of Brand L's dishwasher was not stainless steel! 3. The cycle and method used for washing bottles (see photo). Plus some TMI. First, I gathered all the bottles at once and ran about 8 of them. I kept the used bottles in a washing container filled with detergent. I ran the dishwasher about 1-2 times a day, pre-washing them before putting them in. Since I was also pumping for mixed feeding, the dishwashing was no joke. (Is it just breast milk?). Newborns produce a huge amount of bottles, so I put them in the dishwasher and ran it, and also did boiling water sterilization once a day. I heard that dishwasher sterilization involves rinsing and drying at a total temperature of 75 degrees, so since my baby was a newborn, I also regularly sterilized the bottles in boiling water at 100 degrees. I am doing this in parallel because my baby is not yet 100 days old. (After the baby was 80 days old, I used dishwasher-washed bottles up to twice, and for the third use, I sterilized the washed bottles in boiling water. After 100 days, I plan to increase the frequency to 1-2 times a week for boiling water sterilization.) I calculated the time it takes for the dishwasher to run and the bottles to air dry. I had 9 bottles (160-200ml capacity) on hand, and 3 of them were large Lansino bottles (240ml). When the amount of formula I prepared per feeding was around 165ml, I just used them together, so I used a total of 12 bottles. As the baby grew and the intervals between feedings increased to 5-6 times a day, I think I ended up washing the bottles every two days. In the beginning, when I used a lot of bottles, if the bottles weren't completely dry after the dishwasher run and I was in a hurry, I would run the dishwasher, pour boiling water from a formula kettle into the bottles and nipples to rinse them once, and then warm up formula or pumped breast milk to feed them. I used Spectra bottles at the postpartum care center, so to ensure my baby wouldn't have trouble adjusting to the nipples when we came home, I used Spectra bottles and a breast pump (for mixed feeding). I also used Lansinoh glass bottles. Glass bottles tend to dry quickly and get nice and warm. (I plan to switch to glass bottles when I upgrade the model.) I used Mother-K liquid dishwasher detergent. On days when I did a thorough pre-wash, I used the rapid mode (29 minutes) and added an extra rinse (available once). (I also frequently use the combination of rapid + high-temperature sterilization + powerful drying; it takes 71 minutes). After the wash cycle finished, I selected the bottle sterilization cycle (a function that does not add detergent). On days when I did a pre-wash almost as well as a full wash? I sometimes just ran the bottle sterilization cycle plus an extra rinse (53 minutes), and this cycle does not add detergent separately. Comments (English): [ I bought this to use exclusively for the baby, such as baby bottles, after giving birth. ] || ---------------- || This is a review written after using the product for about three months since its installation on October 9th. I purchased this before my baby was born to sterilize baby bottles and use it exclusively for baby-related items. I intend to run it exclusively for baby-related tasks. I have run it with baby bottles and clean, contaminated glass plates or bowls. Going forward, this dishwasher will handle the washing up that will come with introducing solid foods. Regarding after-sales service and estimated product lifespan: The product warranty is 1 year, the parts retention period is 5 years, and two core motor components are covered by warranties of 3 and 10 years. I chose this dishwasher with the intention of using it for about 4 to 5 years, and I am satisfied with both the price and performance. Since it is a new model and the parts retention period is up to 5 years, I decided to consider that to be a significant amount of use. 1. Installation: All the installation technicians were kind, and they called me between 7 PM and 8 PM the day before installation. They kept their appointments well, and most importantly, they installed it meticulously and explained how to use it. They installed it with a microfiber cloth placed on the floor to prevent scratches or dents. We opted for a drilled installation; although it would have been possible to run the wires through the baseboard under the sink without drilling, they advised that we would need to drill into the drawers or similar areas to secure the wires. So, we drilled into the sink. Before purchasing, I measured the dimensions and secured a spot before ordering. I installed it away from the gas stove, and while it turned out to be larger than expected, I am satisfied. 2. Background of Purchase. With childbirth approaching, I debated whether to buy a U-Pang or a dedicated steam sterilizer for baby bottles, or to purchase a small dishwasher to use for a long time. Boiling water sterilization is recommended for newborn bottles for at least 100 days, so that was another concern. Ultimately, after much deliberation, I purchased a dishwasher and am using it well. Before buying, I compared it with a product from Brand L, and I chose this one because it is hygienic; the interior of the dishwasher, excluding the bottom section, is made of stainless steel. The upper interior of Brand L's dishwasher was not stainless steel! 3. The cycle and method used for washing bottles (see photo). Plus some TMI. First, I gathered all the bottles at once and ran about 8 of them. I kept the used bottles in a washing container filled with detergent. I ran the dishwasher about 1-2 times a day, pre-washing them before putting them in. Since I was also pumping for mixed feeding, the dishwashing was no joke. (Is it just breast milk?). Newborns produce a huge amount of bottles, so I put them in the dishwasher and ran it, and also did boiling water sterilization once a day. I heard that dishwasher sterilization involves rinsing and drying at a total temperature of 75 degrees, so since my baby was a newborn, I also regularly sterilized the bottles in boiling water at 100 degrees. I am doing this in parallel because my baby is not yet 100 days old. (After the baby was 80 days old, I used dishwasher-washed bottles up to twice, and for the third use, I sterilized the washed bottles in boiling water. After 100 days, I plan to increase the frequency to 1-2 times a week for boiling water sterilization.) I calculated the time it takes for the dishwasher to run and the bottles to air dry. I had 9 bottles (160-200ml capacity) on hand, and 3 of them were large Lansino bottles (240ml). When the amount of formula I prepared per feeding was around 165ml, I just used them together, so I used a total of 12 bottles. As the baby grew and the intervals between feedings increased to 5-6 times a day, I think I ended up washing the bottles every two days. In the beginning, when I used a lot of bottles, if the bottles weren't completely dry after the dishwasher run and I was in a hurry, I would run the dishwasher, pour boiling water from a formula kettle into the bottles and nipples to rinse them once, and then warm up formula or pumped breast milk to feed them. I used Spectra bottles at the postpartum care center, so to ensure my baby wouldn't have trouble adjusting to the nipples when we came home, I used Spectra bottles and a breast pump (for mixed feeding). I also used Lansinoh glass bottles. Glass bottles tend to dry quickly and get nice and warm. (I plan to switch to glass bottles when I upgrade the model.) I used Mother-K liquid dishwasher detergent. On days when I did a thorough pre-wash, I used the rapid mode (29 minutes) and added an extra rinse (available once). (I also frequently use the combination of rapid + high-temperature sterilization + powerful drying; it takes 71 minutes). After the wash cycle finished, I selected the bottle sterilization cycle (a function that does not add detergent). On days when I did a pre-wash almost as well as a full wash? I sometimes just ran the bottle sterilization cycle plus an extra rinse (53 minutes), and this cycle does not add detergent separately. So, if I had washed the bottles thoroughly in the sink, I would either run the bottle sterilization cycle instead of the boiling water sterilization cycle, or I would do a quick pre-wash, select a rapid or standard wash cycle to clean the bottles, and then run the sterilization cycle again once finished. When I was feeling lazy, I would run the standard cycle (68 minutes) and add the powerful drying cycle. Tip! If you select the drying mode, pause it briefly after the wash is finished, open the door to shake off the water from the bottles, nipples, and accessories in the basket, and then run the drying cycle; they will be much drier then. Once it finishes, open the door a little later to take them out, move them to a drying rack, and air dry them naturally for faster drying. I put nipples and consumables in a separate basket because they tend to fly around inside when running. Since they don't dry completely after the cycle, I transferred them to a drying rack to air dry before using them again. Advantages: High-temperature sterilization is possible (however, high-temperature sterilization cannot be selected for the bottle or drum sterilization cycles). You can wash all baby items inside (make sure to check if the cycle is dishwasher-safe before putting items in; otherwise, they will shrink). If you put dishes in and use the powerful drying function, they dry well (curved items might retain some moisture inside, but everything else dries well and feels nice and warm). The door opens automatically after the wash is finished (some models do not open automatically, but the Bespoke model does). It is suitable for washing dishes left over after a meal for two. It didn't hold that little. (Glass food containers, clean dishes, cutlery, etc. I sometimes sterilize items with hot water, but I tried putting them in the dishwasher after a pre-wash a few times and it was fine. I checked how much it actually holds). It seems like it will be useful for washing baby food dishes and things like that. After about 20 uses, an alarm automatically pops up on the dishwasher display saying that drum sterilization is needed, and it is hygienic because it has a drum sterilization function (some models do not display this). Once the dishwasher finishes, the liquid detergent dispenser opens automatically (some models do not open). The noise level is not loud by my standards. The dishwasher basket comes out easily as a whole, and there is no difficulty putting it back in (some models are difficult to clean the inside because they don't come out or fit together well). Downside: Nowadays, they don't provide paper manuals; I downloaded the manual via the single-page QR code provided. I think it might be a bit difficult for elderly people to familiarize themselves with how to use it. Also, before purchasing, I was debating between a model with a hot air drying function (DW30CB300C model) and the model I have now installed. I ended up buying this one. Sometimes I wish it had a function to dry things thoroughly. I do wonder if I should have bought a different model. (But I heard that other models are almost the same and don't dry things thoroughly). Still, since it has a drying function, dishes with wide surfaces are mostly dry. (PPSU bottles don't dry all the way through, so you need to move them to a separate drying rack.) In my experience, moisture stays inside the dishwasher for a long time. Even when I leave the door open, I have to leave it open for several days for the inside to dry completely. (If you use it every day, you might not mind; since I only run the baby's items these days and only use it once every two days, the moisture bothered me.) I don't think the large dishwasher I used before was like this, so maybe it's because this is a small one. Overall, I am satisfied with it. Additional review after the baby turned 100 days. First, I do boiling water sterilization once a week these days. Then, I roughly wash things and use the Standard + High Temperature Sterilization + Extra Rinse + Power Dry (takes 1 hour and 41 minutes) cycle the most. I hardly use the separate bottle sterilization course anymore. I run it for everything related to the baby, such as bottles, teething toys, and pacifiers. I run the dishwasher once every 2 to 3 days. (Feeding intervals are 4 hours, using 4 bottles a day). When the dishwasher starts and there are 30 minutes left, it is the "Power Dry" time. It doesn't blow hot air or a breeze; instead, it works like a hair dryer. The principle is that water at a high temperature of over 70 degrees is sprayed, and that heat is transferred to the dishes to dry them. Dishes, plates, and glass, which retain thermal energy well, dry quickly, but plastics do not. (I checked the post on the Samsung Electronics website asking how to dry them well). I stop the dishwasher when there are 10 to 15 minutes left on the Power Dry timer. When I open the door, a lot of hot steam comes out. I organize the nipples, accessories, and bottles inside (shake off the water), put them back in properly, and press start. Once it is finished, the dishwasher door opens, and I move the items to the bottle drying rack to air dry. I wanted to share this in case anyone thought Power Dry just blows out air. No matter how much I think about it, I feel like I made the right purchase for my needs! Good luck with parenting! April 7, 2025 [Updated Review] The baby is over 172 days old (approaching 6 months). I have uploaded additional photos. I am reverently preparing and practicing solid foods. Why are there so many containers and tools? It is very, very good. I really think I made a great purchase! Bottles, teething toys, pacifiers, silicone medicine bottles, and even sucking toys made of dishwasher-safe materials—I put everything in there to wash and sterilize it. I am satisfied! If my honest review of a product I bought with my own money was helpful, please press the like button~

(생후 80일 지나고 부턴 2번까지 젖병 식세기 돌린걸로 쓰고, 3번째 쓸때는 세척된 젖병들 열탕소독 함, 100일 지나면 주 1~2회 정도로 텀 늘려서 열탕소독 예정)식세기 돌아가고 자연건조 되는 시간. 고려해서 돌렸었구요. 젖병 9개(160~200ml용량) 구비했고, 3개는 란시노 큰거(240ml)인데 1회 분유타는 량이 165ml 정도로 되었을땐 걍 같이 써서 젖병 총 12개 사용했습니다. 애기가 커서 하루 5~6번 수유로 텀이 늘다보니 2일에 1번으로 젖병 세척돌리게 된거 같아요.초반에 젖병 많이 쓸때는.. 식세기 돌리고 젖병 건조가 덜되서 급할땐 식세기 돌아가고 분유포트 끓인물 젖병이랑 젖꼭지에 넣코 한번 헹구고 분유나 유축모유 데워서 줬어요.저는 조리원에서 스펙트라 젖병을 써서 아기 집에왔을때 젖꼭지 적응 힘들지 말라고 스펙트라 젖병이랑 유축기(혼합수유함) 썼어요.그리고 같이 란시노 유리젖병도 썼습니다.  유리젖병은 빨리 마르는 편이고 뜨끈뜨끈 합니다. (단계업하면 다 유리젖병으로 교체예정)세제는 마더케이 액상식세기 세제 사용했습니다. 꼼꼼하게 애벌세척을 했던 날은, 급속모드(29분)를 사용하고 헹굼추가(1회 가능)를 했습니다. (급속+고온살균+강력건조 이 조합도 잘씀 71분 뜸)그리고 나서 세척 코스가 끝나면, 그 다음 젖병살균코스(세제투입 안되는 기능임)를 선택했어요. 애벌세척을 거의 세척급으로 잘한날은?그냥 젖병살균코스+헹굼추가(53분)만 돌리기도 했는데, 이 코스는 세제가 따로 투입되거나 하지 않아요.그래서 따로 싱크대에서 세척을 잘 했으면, 젖병살균 코스만 열탕소독 대신 개념으로 돌리던가, 아니면 애벌세척 대충하고, 급속이나 표준으로 세척코스를 선택해 젖병을 씻고, 끝나면 다시 살균코스를 돌리는 방법을 택했습니다.영 귀찮을땐, 표준(68분)으로 돌리고, 강력건조를 추가했어요. 팁!! 건조모드 선택하면 세척 끝나면 그때 잠시 정지 후 열고 젖병이랑 젖꼭지 부속품들 바스켓에 넣어둔거 물기 탈탈 털어주고 건조모드 돌리면 그나마 많이 말라있어요. 종료되면 문 좀 늦게 열고 꺼내서 젖병 건조대 이동 후 자연 건조시 빨리 마름.젖꼭지나 소모품은 돌리면 여기저기 내부에서 튀어다녀서 별도 바스켓에 넣어서 돌렸어요. 다 돌아가고 나면 뽀송하게 바싹 안마르기 때문에 따로 건조대로 옮겨서 말려주고 사용했습니다. ✅️장점고온살균이 가능해요. (단 젖병살균 통살균 코스로는 고온살균이 선택이 안됩니다)아기 용품들 다 넣어서 세척이 가능해요(넣기전에 식세기 사용해도 되는 코스인지 꼭 확인하고 돌리세요. 안그러면서 쪼그라듭니다. )그릇 등 넣고 강력건조 기능쓰면 잘 말라요.(굴곡진 것들은 안에 물기가 좀 남아있고, 그 외에는 잘 말라있음 뜨끈뜨끈함)세척이 끝나고 자동으로 문이 열려요(일부 안열리는 모델들이 있음, 비스포크는 열림)2인 식사후 나오는 그릇 등 세척하기에 적합해요. 그렇케 조금 들어가지 않았어요. (유리 락앤락 반찬통들, 깨끗한 그릇들, 수저 식기류들 등.. 가끔 뜨거운물로 소독하는데, 애벌세척 후 식세기에 넣어서 몇번 써보니까 괜찮았어요. 얼마나 들어가나 봄)이유식 그릇 등 돌릴때 유용할꺼 같습니다. 20회 정도 사용하고 나면, 식세기 디스플레이에 자동으로 통살균 필요하다고 알람이 뜨고 통살균 기능이 있어서 위생적이에요.(안뜨는 기기들도 있음.)식세기 다 돌아가고 나면 액상 세제 투입기가 자동으로 열려있음 (안열리는 모델도 있음)소음이 내기준 크지 않음. 식세기 바스켓 통째로 잘빼지고 다시 끼는데 어려움 없음.( 잘 안빼지고 안껴져서 내부 청소하기 힘든 모델들이 있음..)✅️단점설명서가 요즘은 종이로 안줌, 주신 한장짜리 큐알 들어가서 설명서 다운받았어요. 어르신들이 사용법을 숙지하시기에는 좀 어려움이 있으실꺼 같습니다. 또 구매전에 열풍건조기능이 있는 제품(DW30CB300C모델)이랑 지금 설치한 모델이랑 고민을 했었는데.. 이거로 구매했고.가끔 바싹 말려주는 기능이 있으면 좋켔다.. 다른 모델로 샀으면 어땠을까? 생각이 들긴하더라구요. (근데 다른 모델도 거의 똑같데요 바싹 안말려준데요)그래도 건조기능이 있어서 표면이 넓은 그릇들은 거의 말라있긴 합니다. (ppsu 젖병은 속까지 안말라요.. 따로 건조대 이동 필요함)식세기 기기 내부에 물기가 내기준 오래 있어요. 문열고 있어도 몇일을 열어놔야 안이 바싹 마르더라구요... (매일 쓰면 신경 안쓸 수 있음, 요즘 애기꺼만 돌리다보니 2일에 1회 써서 물기들이 신경쓰였음) 이전에 쓰던 대형 식세기는 안그랬던거 같은데, 소형이라 그런가봐요;;전반적으로 만족하며 사용하고 있습니다.✅️ 아기 100일  지나고 추가후기우선 요즘 열탕소독을 주1회 합니다.그리고 대강 씻어서 표준+고온살균+헹굼추가+강력건조( 1시간 41분 뜸)를. 제일 많이 씁니다. 따로 젖병살균코스는 이제 거의 안쓰게 되네용. 젖병 치발기 쪽쪽이 애기에 대한거 다 돌립니다. 2~3일에 1번씩 식세기 돌려요. (수유텀 4시간, 젖병 1일 4병 사용함)식세기 돌아가고 마지막 30분 남았을때 강력건조 시간인데건조 열풍이나 바람이 나오는게 아니고, 드라이기 말리는 형식으로, 고온 70도 이상물이 뿌려지고 그 열기가 식기로 전달되어 건조되는 원리랍니다. 열에너지를 잘가지고 있는 그릇 접시 유리들은 빨리건조되고, 플라스틱 들은 그렇치 못해요ㅜ.ㅜ .(삼성전자 사이트에서 건조가 잘되는법을 알려주세요 글 확인함)강력건조한 건조시간 10~15분 남았을때 정지 후. 문열면 뜨거운 김, 수증기가 많이 나와요. 안에 젖꼭지 부속품들 젖병 등 정리(물기털기)를 하고 다시 바르게 넣코 시작 누른 뒤. 다 끝나면 식세기 문이 열리고, 젖병건조대로 옮겨서 자연건조 시키고 있어용.혹시 강력건조가 바람나온다고 생각하실까봐 공유드리구요.계속 생각해도 목적에 맞게 잘산거 같아요!육아 홧팅입니다!✅️ 25년 4월 7일 추가후기 아기는 생후 172일 넘음 (6개월 되어감) 추가사진 업로드함.이유식을 경건하게 준비 및 연습하는데.. 이유식 용기들 도구들 왜케 많이나오죠.. 매우 매우 좋습니다. 진짜 잘산거 같아요!젖병들도 치발기 쪽쪽이 실리콘약병.. 식세기 넣어도 되는 소재의 빠는 장난감들.. 모두모두 잘 넣어서 씻고 살균합니다. 만족합니다! 저의 내돈내산 솔찍 리뷰가 도움 되셨다면 좋아요 꾸욱 눌러주세요~❤️

Comments (English): [ I bought this to use exclusively for the baby, such as baby bottles, after giving birth. ] || ---------------- || This is a review written after using the product for about three months since its installation on October 9th. I purchased this before my baby was born to sterilize baby bottles and use it exclusively for baby-related items. I intend to run it exclusively for baby-related tasks. I have run it with baby bottles and clean, contaminated glass plates or bowls. Going forward, this dishwasher will handle the washing up that will come with introducing solid foods. Regarding after-sales service and estimated product lifespan: The product warranty is 1 year, the parts retention period is 5 years, and two core motor components are covered by warranties of 3 and 10 years. I chose this dishwasher with the intention of using it for about 4 to 5 years, and I am satisfied with both the price and performance. Since it is a new model and the parts retention period is up to 5 years, I decided to consider that to be a significant amount of use. 1. Installation: All the installation technicians were kind, and they called me between 7 PM and 8 PM the day before installation. They kept their appointments well, and most importantly, they installed it meticulously and explained how to use it. They installed it with a microfiber cloth placed on the floor to prevent scratches or dents. We opted for a drilled installation; although it would have been possible to run the wires through the baseboard under the sink without drilling, they advised that we would need to drill into the drawers or similar areas to secure the wires. So, we drilled into the sink. Before purchasing, I measured the dimensions and secured a spot before ordering. I installed it away from the gas stove, and while it turned out to be larger than expected, I am satisfied. 2. Background of Purchase. With childbirth approaching, I debated whether to buy a U-Pang or a dedicated steam sterilizer for baby bottles, or to purchase a small dishwasher to use for a long time. Boiling water sterilization is recommended for newborn bottles for at least 100 days, so that was another concern. Ultimately, after much deliberation, I purchased a dishwasher and am using it well. Before buying, I compared it with a product from Brand L, and I chose this one because it is hygienic; the interior of the dishwasher, excluding the bottom section, is made of stainless steel. The upper interior of Brand L's dishwasher was not stainless steel! 3. The cycle and method used for washing bottles (see photo). Plus some TMI. First, I gathered all the bottles at once and ran about 8 of them. I kept the used bottles in a washing container filled with detergent. I ran the dishwasher about 1-2 times a day, pre-washing them before putting them in. Since I was also pumping for mixed feeding, the dishwashing was no joke. (Is it just breast milk?). Newborns produce a huge amount of bottles, so I put them in the dishwasher and ran it, and also did boiling water sterilization once a day. I heard that dishwasher sterilization involves rinsing and drying at a total temperature of 75 degrees, so since my baby was a newborn, I also regularly sterilized the bottles in boiling water at 100 degrees. I am doing this in parallel because my baby is not yet 100 days old. (After the baby was 80 days old, I used dishwasher-washed bottles up to twice, and for the third use, I sterilized the washed bottles in boiling water. After 100 days, I plan to increase the frequency to 1-2 times a week for boiling water sterilization.) I calculated the time it takes for the dishwasher to run and the bottles to air dry. I had 9 bottles (160-200ml capacity) on hand, and 3 of them were large Lansino bottles (240ml). When the amount of formula I prepared per feeding was around 165ml, I just used them together, so I used a total of 12 bottles. As the baby grew and the intervals between feedings increased to 5-6 times a day, I think I ended up washing the bottles every two days. In the beginning, when I used a lot of bottles, if the bottles weren't completely dry after the dishwasher run and I was in a hurry, I would run the dishwasher, pour boiling water from a formula kettle into the bottles and nipples to rinse them once, and then warm up formula or pumped breast milk to feed them. I used Spectra bottles at the postpartum care center, so to ensure my baby wouldn't have trouble adjusting to the nipples when we came home, I used Spectra bottles and a breast pump (for mixed feeding). I also used Lansinoh glass bottles. Glass bottles tend to dry quickly and get nice and warm. (I plan to switch to glass bottles when I upgrade the model.) I used Mother-K liquid dishwasher detergent. On days when I did a thorough pre-wash, I used the rapid mode (29 minutes) and added an extra rinse (available once). (I also frequently use the combination of rapid + high-temperature sterilization + powerful drying; it takes 71 minutes). After the wash cycle finished, I selected the bottle sterilization cycle (a function that does not add detergent). On days when I did a pre-wash almost as well as a full wash? I sometimes just ran the bottle sterilization cycle plus an extra rinse (53 minutes), and this cycle does not add detergent separately. So, if I had washed the bottles thoroughly in the sink, I would either run the bottle sterilization cycle instead of the boiling water sterilization cycle, or I would do a quick pre-wash, select a rapid or standard wash cycle to clean the bottles, and then run the sterilization cycle again once finished. When I was feeling lazy, I would run the standard cycle (68 minutes) and add the powerful drying cycle. Tip! If you select the drying mode, pause it briefly after the wash is finished, open the door to shake off the water from the bottles, nipples, and accessories in the basket, and then run the drying cycle; they will be much drier then. Once it finishes, open the door a little later to take them out, move them to a drying rack, and air dry them naturally for faster drying. I put nipples and consumables in a separate basket because they tend to fly around inside when running. Since they don't dry completely after the cycle, I transferred them to a drying rack to air dry before using them again. Advantages: High-temperature sterilization is possible (however, high-temperature sterilization cannot be selected for the bottle or drum sterilization cycles). You can wash all baby items inside (make sure to check if the cycle is dishwasher-safe before putting items in; otherwise, they will shrink). If you put dishes in and use the powerful drying function, they dry well (curved items might retain some moisture inside, but everything else dries well and feels nice and warm). The door opens automatically after the wash is finished (some models do not open automatically, but the Bespoke model does). It is suitable for washing dishes left over after a meal for two. It didn't hold that little. (Glass food containers, clean dishes, cutlery, etc. I sometimes sterilize items with hot water, but I tried putting them in the dishwasher after a pre-wash a few times and it was fine. I checked how much it actually holds). It seems like it will be useful for washing baby food dishes and things like that. After about 20 uses, an alarm automatically pops up on the dishwasher display saying that drum sterilization is needed, and it is hygienic because it has a drum sterilization function (some models do not display this). Once the dishwasher finishes, the liquid detergent dispenser opens automatically (some models do not open). The noise level is not loud by my standards. The dishwasher basket comes out easily as a whole, and there is no difficulty putting it back in (some models are difficult to clean the inside because they don't come out or fit together well). Downside: Nowadays, they don't provide paper manuals; I downloaded the manual via the single-page QR code provided. I think it might be a bit difficult for elderly people to familiarize themselves with how to use it. Also, before purchasing, I was debating between a model with a hot air drying function (DW30CB300C model) and the model I have now installed. I ended up buying this one. Sometimes I wish it had a function to dry things thoroughly. I do wonder if I should have bought a different model. (But I heard that other models are almost the same and don't dry things thoroughly). Still, since it has a drying function, dishes with wide surfaces are mostly dry. (PPSU bottles don't dry all the way through, so you need to move them to a separate drying rack.) In my experience, moisture stays inside the dishwasher for a long time. Even when I leave the door open, I have to leave it open for several days for the inside to dry completely. (If you use it every day, you might not mind; since I only run the baby's items these days and only use it once every two days, the moisture bothered me.) I don't think the large dishwasher I used before was like this, so maybe it's because this is a small one. Overall, I am satisfied with it. Additional review after the baby turned 100 days. First, I do boiling water sterilization once a week these days. Then, I roughly wash things and use the Standard + High Temperature Sterilization + Extra Rinse + Power Dry (takes 1 hour and 41 minutes) cycle the most. I hardly use the separate bottle sterilization course anymore. I run it for everything related to the baby, such as bottles, teething toys, and pacifiers. I run the dishwasher once every 2 to 3 days. (Feeding intervals are 4 hours, using 4 bottles a day). When the dishwasher starts and there are 30 minutes left, it is the "Power Dry" time. It doesn't blow hot air or a breeze; instead, it works like a hair dryer. The principle is that water at a high temperature of over 70 degrees is sprayed, and that heat is transferred to the dishes to dry them. Dishes, plates, and glass, which retain thermal energy well, dry quickly, but plastics do not. (I checked the post on the Samsung Electronics website asking how to dry them well). I stop the dishwasher when there are 10 to 15 minutes left on the Power Dry timer. When I open the door, a lot of hot steam comes out. I organize the nipples, accessories, and bottles inside (shake off the water), put them back in properly, and press start. Once it is finished, the dishwasher door opens, and I move the items to the bottle drying rack to air dry. I wanted to share this in case anyone thought Power Dry just blows out air. No matter how much I think about it, I feel like I made the right purchase for my needs! Good luck with parenting! April 7, 2025 [Updated Review] The baby is over 172 days old (approaching 6 months). I have uploaded additional photos. I am reverently preparing and practicing solid foods. Why are there so many containers and tools? It is very, very good. I really think I made a great purchase! Comments (English): [ I bought this to use exclusively for the baby, such as baby bottles, after giving birth. ] || ---------------- || This is a review written after using the product for about three months since its installation on October 9th. I purchased this before my baby was born to sterilize baby bottles and use it exclusively for baby-related items. I intend to run it exclusively for baby-related tasks. I have run it with baby bottles and clean, contaminated glass plates or bowls. Going forward, this dishwasher will handle the washing up that will come with introducing solid foods. Regarding after-sales service and estimated product lifespan: The product warranty is 1 year, the parts retention period is 5 years, and two core motor components are covered by warranties of 3 and 10 years. I chose this dishwasher with the intention of using it for about 4 to 5 years, and I am satisfied with both the price and performance. Since it is a new model and the parts retention period is up to 5 years, I decided to consider that to be a significant amount of use. 1. Installation: All the installation technicians were kind, and they called me between 7 PM and 8 PM the day before installation. They kept their appointments well, and most importantly, they installed it meticulously and explained how to use it. They installed it with a microfiber cloth placed on the floor to prevent scratches or dents. We opted for a drilled installation; although it would have been possible to run the wires through the baseboard under the sink without drilling, they advised that we would need to drill into the drawers or similar areas to secure the wires. So, we drilled into the sink. Before purchasing, I measured the dimensions and secured a spot before ordering. I installed it away from the gas stove, and while it turned out to be larger than expected, I am satisfied. 2. Background of Purchase. With childbirth approaching, I debated whether to buy a U-Pang or a dedicated steam sterilizer for baby bottles, or to purchase a small dishwasher to use for a long time. Boiling water sterilization is recommended for newborn bottles for at least 100 days, so that was another concern. Ultimately, after much deliberation, I purchased a dishwasher and am using it well. Before buying, I compared it with a product from Brand L, and I chose this one because it is hygienic; the interior of the dishwasher, excluding the bottom section, is made of stainless steel. The upper interior of Brand L's dishwasher was not stainless steel! 3. The cycle and method used for washing bottles (see photo). Plus some TMI. First, I gathered all the bottles at once and ran about 8 of them. I kept the used bottles in a washing container filled with detergent. I ran the dishwasher about 1-2 times a day, pre-washing them before putting them in. Since I was also pumping for mixed feeding, the dishwashing was no joke. (Is it just breast milk?). Newborns produce a huge amount of bottles, so I put them in the dishwasher and ran it, and also did boiling water sterilization once a day. I heard that dishwasher sterilization involves rinsing and drying at a total temperature of 75 degrees, so since my baby was a newborn, I also regularly sterilized the bottles in boiling water at 100 degrees. I am doing this in parallel because my baby is not yet 100 days old. (After the baby was 80 days old, I used dishwasher-washed bottles up to twice, and for the third use, I sterilized the washed bottles in boiling water. After 100 days, I plan to increase the frequency to 1-2 times a week for boiling water sterilization.) I calculated the time it takes for the dishwasher to run and the bottles to air dry. I had 9 bottles (160-200ml capacity) on hand, and 3 of them were large Lansino bottles (240ml). When the amount of formula I prepared per feeding was around 165ml, I just used them together, so I used a total of 12 bottles. As the baby grew and the intervals between feedings increased to 5-6 times a day, I think I ended up washing the bottles every two days. In the beginning, when I used a lot of bottles, if the bottles weren't completely dry after the dishwasher run and I was in a hurry, I would run the dishwasher, pour boiling water from a formula kettle into the bottles and nipples to rinse them once, and then warm up formula or pumped breast milk to feed them. I used Spectra bottles at the postpartum care center, so to ensure my baby wouldn't have trouble adjusting to the nipples when we came home, I used Spectra bottles and a breast pump (for mixed feeding). I also used Lansinoh glass bottles. Glass bottles tend to dry quickly and get nice and warm. (I plan to switch to glass bottles when I upgrade the model.) I used Mother-K liquid dishwasher detergent. On days when I did a thorough pre-wash, I used the rapid mode (29 minutes) and added an extra rinse (available once). (I also frequently use the combination of rapid + high-temperature sterilization + powerful drying; it takes 71 minutes). Sentence (English): I really think I made a great purchase!
Comments (English): [ I bought this to use exclusively for the baby, such as baby bottles, after giving birth. ] || ---------------- || This is a review written after using the product for about three months since its installation on October 9th. I purchased this before my baby was born to sterilize baby bottles and use it exclusively for baby-related items. I intend to run it exclusively for baby-related tasks. I have run it with baby bottles and clean, contaminated glass plates or bowls. Going forward, this dishwasher will handle the washing up that will come with introducing solid foods. Regarding after-sales service and estimated product lifespan: The product warranty is 1 year, the parts retention period is 5 years, and two core motor components are covered by warranties of 3 and 10 years. I chose this dishwasher with the intention of using it for about 4 to 5 years, and I am satisfied with both the price and performance. Since it is a new model and the parts retention period is up to 5 years, I decided to consider that to be a significant amount of use. 1. Installation: All the installation technicians were kind, and they called me between 7 PM and 8 PM the day before installation. They kept their appointments well, and most importantly, they installed it meticulously and explained how to use it. They installed it with a microfiber cloth placed on the floor to prevent scratches or dents. We opted for a drilled installation; although it would have been possible to run the wires through the baseboard under the sink without drilling, they advised that we would need to drill into the drawers or similar areas to secure the wires. So, we drilled into the sink. Before purchasing, I measured the dimensions and secured a spot before ordering. I installed it away from the gas stove, and while it turned out to be larger than expected, I am satisfied. 2. Background of Purchase. With childbirth approaching, I debated whether to buy a U-Pang or a dedicated steam sterilizer for baby bottles, or to purchase a small dishwasher to use for a long time. Boiling water sterilization is recommended for newborn bottles for at least 100 days, so that was another concern. Ultimately, after much deliberation, I purchased a dishwasher and am using it well. Before buying, I compared it with a product from Brand L, and I chose this one because it is hygienic; the interior of the dishwasher, excluding the bottom section, is made of stainless steel. The upper interior of Brand L's dishwasher was not stainless steel! 3. The cycle and method used for washing bottles (see photo). Plus some TMI. First, I gathered all the bottles at once and ran about 8 of them. I kept the used bottles in a washing container filled with detergent. I ran the dishwasher about 1-2 times a day, pre-washing them before putting them in. Since I was also pumping for mixed feeding, the dishwashing was no joke. (Is it just breast milk?). Newborns produce a huge amount of bottles, so I put them in the dishwasher and ran it, and also did boiling water sterilization once a day. I heard that dishwasher sterilization involves rinsing and drying at a total temperature of 75 degrees, so since my baby was a newborn, I also regularly sterilized the bottles in boiling water at 100 degrees. I am doing this in parallel because my baby is not yet 100 days old. (After the baby was 80 days old, I used dishwasher-washed bottles up to twice, and for the third use, I sterilized the washed bottles in boiling water. After 100 days, I plan to increase the frequency to 1-2 times a week for boiling water sterilization.) I calculated the time it takes for the dishwasher to run and the bottles to air dry. I had 9 bottles (160-200ml capacity) on hand, and 3 of them were large Lansino bottles (240ml). When the amount of formula I prepared per feeding was around 165ml, I just used them together, so I used a total of 12 bottles. As the baby grew and the intervals between feedings increased to 5-6 times a day, I think I ended up washing the bottles every two days. In the beginning, when I used a lot of bottles, if the bottles weren't completely dry after the dishwasher run and I was in a hurry, I would run the dishwasher, pour boiling water from a formula kettle into the bottles and nipples to rinse them once, and then warm up formula or pumped breast milk to feed them. I used Spectra bottles at the postpartum care center, so to ensure my baby wouldn't have trouble adjusting to the nipples when we came home, I used Spectra bottles and a breast pump (for mixed feeding). I also used Lansinoh glass bottles. Glass bottles tend to dry quickly and get nice and warm. (I plan to switch to glass bottles when I upgrade the model.) I used Mother-K liquid dishwasher detergent. On days when I did a thorough pre-wash, I used the rapid mode (29 minutes) and added an extra rinse (available once). (I also frequently use the combination of rapid + high-temperature sterilization + powerful drying; it takes 71 minutes). After the wash cycle finished, I selected the bottle sterilization cycle (a function that does not add detergent). On days when I did a pre-wash almost as well as a full wash? I sometimes just ran the bottle sterilization cycle plus an extra rinse (53 minutes), and this cycle does not add detergent separately. So, if I had washed the bottles thoroughly in the sink, I would either run the bottle sterilization cycle instead of the boiling water sterilization cycle, or I would do a quick pre-wash, select a rapid or standard wash cycle to clean the bottles, and then run the sterilization cycle again once finished. When I was feeling lazy, I would run the standard cycle (68 minutes) and add the powerful drying cycle. Tip! If you select the drying mode, pause it briefly after the wash is finished, open the door to shake off the water from the bottles, nipples, and accessories in the basket, and then run the drying cycle; they will be much drier then. Once it finishes, open the door a little later to take them out, move them to a drying rack, and air dry them naturally for faster drying. I put nipples and consumables in a separate basket because they tend to fly around inside when running. Since they don't dry completely after the cycle, I transferred them to a drying rack to air dry before using them again. Advantages: High-temperature sterilization is possible (however, high-temperature sterilization cannot be selected for the bottle or drum sterilization cycles). You can wash all baby items inside (make sure to check if the cycle is dishwasher-safe before putting items in; otherwise, they will shrink). If you put dishes in and use the powerful drying function, they dry well (curved items might retain some moisture inside, but everything else dries well and feels nice and warm). The door opens automatically after the wash is finished (some models do not open automatically, but the Bespoke model does). It is suitable for washing dishes left over after a meal for two. It didn't hold that little. (Glass food containers, clean dishes, cutlery, etc. I sometimes sterilize items with hot water, but I tried putting them in the dishwasher after a pre-wash a few times and it was fine. I checked how much it actually holds). It seems like it will be useful for washing baby food dishes and things like that. After about 20 uses, an alarm automatically pops up on the dishwasher display saying that drum sterilization is needed, and it is hygienic because it has a drum sterilization function (some models do not display this). Once the dishwasher finishes, the liquid detergent dispenser opens automatically (some models do not open). The noise level is not loud by my standards. The dishwasher basket comes out easily as a whole, and there is no difficulty putting it back in (some models are difficult to clean the inside because they don't come out or fit together well). Downside: Nowadays, they don't provide paper manuals; I downloaded the manual via the single-page QR code provided. I think it might be a bit difficult for elderly people to familiarize themselves with how to use it. Also, before purchasing, I was debating between a model with a hot air drying function (DW30CB300C model) and the model I have now installed. I ended up buying this one. Sometimes I wish it had a function to dry things thoroughly. I do wonder if I should have bought a different model. (But I heard that other models are almost the same and don't dry things thoroughly). Still, since it has a drying function, dishes with wide surfaces are mostly dry. (PPSU bottles don't dry all the way through, so you need to move them to a separate drying rack.) In my experience, moisture stays inside the dishwasher for a long time. Even when I leave the door open, I have to leave it open for several days for the inside to dry completely. (If you use it every day, you might not mind; since I only run the baby's items these days and only use it once every two days, the moisture bothered me.) I don't think the large dishwasher I used before was like this, so maybe it's because this is a small one. Overall, I am satisfied with it. Additional review after the baby turned 100 days. First, I do boiling water sterilization once a week these days. Then, I roughly wash things and use the Standard + High Temperature Sterilization + Extra Rinse + Power Dry (takes 1 hour and 41 minutes) cycle the most. I hardly use the separate bottle sterilization course anymore. I run it for everything related to the baby, such as bottles, teething toys, and pacifiers. I run the dishwasher once every 2 to 3 days. (Feeding intervals are 4 hours, using 4 bottles a day). When the dishwasher starts and there are 30 minutes left, it is the "Power Dry" time. It doesn't blow hot air or a breeze; instead, it works like a hair dryer. The principle is that water at a high temperature of over 70 degrees is sprayed, and that heat is transferred to the dishes to dry them. Dishes, plates, and glass, which retain thermal energy well, dry quickly, but plastics do not. (I checked the post on the Samsung Electronics website asking how to dry them well). I stop the dishwasher when there are 10 to 15 minutes left on the Power Dry timer. When I open the door, a lot of hot steam comes out. I organize the nipples, accessories, and bottles inside (shake off the water), put them back in properly, and press start. Once it is finished, the dishwasher door opens, and I move the items to the bottle drying rack to air dry. I wanted to share this in case anyone thought Power Dry just blows out air. No matter how much I think about it, I feel like I made the right purchase for my needs! Good luck with parenting! April 7, 2025 [Updated Review] The baby is over 172 days old (approaching 6 months). I have uploaded additional photos. I am reverently preparing and practicing solid foods. Why are there so many containers and tools? It is very, very good. I really think I made a great purchase! Bottles, teething toys, pacifiers, silicone medicine bottles, and even sucking toys made of dishwasher-safe materials—I put everything in there to wash and sterilize it. I am satisfied! If my honest review of a product I bought with my own money was helpful, please press the like button~
